text:
If you visit Poás Volcano in Costa Rica, you’ll quickly learn that it is notoriously hard to see. Because of its high elevation in the cloud forest, the massive crater is almost always swallowed by a thick blanket of white fog.
​When we first arrived, it was completely clouded over. But we got incredibly lucky

!Our local guide told us about a beautiful Tico (Costa Rican) belief that if you genuinely ask permission from the volcano to see it, the mountain will unveil itself for you.
​It sounds crazy, but we decided to try the magic. We took a moment to quiet down, connect with our surroundings, and literally talked to nature, asking it to show its face.
​And guess what? It actually worked.
​The heavy clouds hung low for a tense 10 minutes, testing our resolve. But we stayed patient. Suddenly, the mist began to swirl and lift, revealing absolutely incredible, jaw-dropping views of the  crater below. It was a surreal, humbling moment that felt entirely spiritual. Some moments are hard to explain!

text:
Frío, árido, imponente.

El Parque Nacional Volcán Irazú es, sin duda, uno de los destinos más emblemáticos de Costa Rica. Como el volcán de mayor elevación del país, siempre ofrece una experiencia memorable, sin importar cuántas veces se visite. He tenido la oportunidad de ir en varias ocasiones y cada visita tiene su propio encanto.

Una de las cosas que más disfruto es su clima tan particular y las vistas que regala. En días despejados, es impresionante poder ver tanto el océano Pacífico como el Atlántico desde un mismo punto. Y cuando está nublado, el manto blanco crea un ambiente único, casi místico, que también tiene su magia.

Aunque los lagos del cráter se secaron hace algunos años, el lugar sigue siendo increíble. Se puede caminar por la esplanada, acercarse al mirador o incluso llegar en carro, lo que lo hace accesible para todo tipo de visitantes. Además, el parque cuenta con cafetería, servicios sanitarios y suficientes espacios de parqueo, lo cual facilita mucho la visita.

Un detalle importante es que las entradas deben comprarse previamente por Internet, algo que conviene tomar en cuenta para planear el paseo sin contratiempos.

En resumen, el Volcán Irazú es un lugar que siempre sorprende, ya sea por su clima, sus panorámicas o su tranquilidad. Es un destino ideal para quienes disfrutan de la naturaleza, la fotografía y los paisajes que solo Costa Rica puede ofrecer.
textTranslated:
Cold, arid, imposing.

Irazú Volcano National Park is undoubtedly one of Costa Rica's most iconic destinations. As the country's highest volcano, it always offers a memorable experience, no matter how many times you visit. I've had the opportunity to go several times, and each visit has its own unique charm.

One of the things I enjoy most is its distinctive climate and the breathtaking views it offers. On clear days, it's stunning to see both the Pacific and Atlantic Oceans from the same vantage point. And when it's cloudy, the blanket of snow creates a unique, almost mystical atmosphere, which also has its own magic.

Although the crater lakes dried up some years ago, the place remains incredible. You can walk along the esplanade, approach the viewpoint, or even drive there, making it accessible to all types of visitors. Furthermore, the park has a cafeteria, restrooms, and ample parking, which greatly facilitates a visit.

An important detail is that tickets must be purchased online in advance, something to keep in mind to plan your trip smoothly.

In short, Irazú Volcano is a place that never fails to surprise, whether for its climate, its panoramic views, or its tranquility. It's an ideal destination for those who enjoy nature, photography, and the landscapes that only Costa Rica can offer.

text: Vstopnico sva kupila vnaprej, saj jo lahko le preko neta, če je nimaš ne moreš vstopiti. To je čisti nateg in poneumljanje ljudi, saj če je vreme oblačno in deževno vidiš le meglo. Denarja za nič ti ne vrne nihče. Ker tam ni signala, je tudi ne moreš kupiti pred vstopom. Midva sva za par sekund sicer videla vulkan, a veliko ljudi za nama in tudi prej ni videlo nič. Slab sistem, kjer je precej očitno le pobiranje denarja tako za vstopnino kot parkirnino. Zelo slabo, tudi ob nični vidljivosti in dežju laziš na rob kraterja kjer se počutiš kot idiot. Pišete popotniki, da dobiš čelado, a midva je nisva in tudi drugi je niso imeli. Na robu kraterja  nisva imela omejitve časa na 20 minut. Bila pa sva v lastni režiji.  Ne priporočam- če bi lahko dala manj kot eno zvezdico, bi dala manj.
textTranslated: We bought the ticket in advance, because you can only get it online, if you don't have it you can't get in. This is a pure scam and a rip-off of people, because if the weather is cloudy and rainy, you can only see fog. No one will refund your money for anything. Since there is no signal there, you can't buy it before entering. We did see the volcano for a few seconds, but many people behind us and before us didn't see anything either. Bad system, where it's pretty obvious that they're just collecting money for both the entrance fee and the parking fee. Very bad, even with zero visibility and rain, you climb to the edge of the crater where you feel like an idiot. Travelers write that you get a helmet, but we didn't and neither did others. We didn't have a 20-minute time limit on the edge of the crater. But we were on our own. I don't recommend it - if I could give less than one star, I would.

textTranslated: Poás Volcano is an active volcano located in central Costa Rica. It is easily accessible, located approximately 50 kilometers northwest of the capital, San Jose. At approximately 2,697–2,708 meters above sea level, it is one of the world's largest active volcanic craters. The crater contains a highly acidic volcanic lake. It has erupted over 40 times since 1828, making it one of the most active volcanoes in Costa Rica. Strong eruptions in April 2017 and April 2025 prompted evacuation orders.

text:
TEXTILES Y VOLCANES
Aquel día de 2013, el Volcán Poás nos recibió con su aliento sulfuroso y su corona de neblina. El cráter, inmenso y vivo, parecía respirar con nosotros—una pausa geológica en medio de nuestras propias transformaciones. A su lado, la Laguna Botos dormía como un espejo verde entre helechos gigantes, testigo silente de encuentros que iban más allá del turismo.

Me acompañaba Gabriel Soler, valenciano de verbo ágil y mirada inquieta, representante de casas textileras españolas como Eysa Confecciones y Encama. Su visita no era casual: venía en busca de nuevos horizontes comerciales, y yo, como textilero de oficio y memoria, le ofrecía mi conocimiento del mercado costarricense sin cobrarle un céntimo. Lo hacía por la amistad cultivada años atrás, cuando Gabriel llegaba a Tienda La Gloria S.A. con sus catálogos bajo el brazo y yo, como comprador oficial, le abría las puertas del negocio con la misma apertura que hoy le ofrecía al paisaje volcánico.

En medio de bromas, caminatas y conversaciones profundas, Gabriel compartía conmigo una preocupación que ya se intuía como profecía: la amenaza silenciosa de China sobre la industria textil española. Me hablaba de las ferias de Valencia, de los 24,000 m² de exposición, de los 3,000 expositores que mostraban lo mejor del diseño ibérico… y de los miles de visitantes chinos que no venían a negociar, sino a observar, fotografiar, copiar. Años después, esa estrategia invisible hundiría una de las industrias más refinadas del mundo en una crisis de costos, producción y financiamiento que ni los más visionarios supieron anticipar.

Para mí, esa visita al Poás coincidía con otra erupción: la de mi vida personal. En pleno proceso de divorcio, con el duelo aún fresco, me refugiaba en retiros espirituales que me ayudaban a sanar y a aceptar. El volcán, con su fuerza contenida, parecía entenderme. Gabriel, sin saberlo del todo, también fue parte de ese proceso de recomienzo.

Las visitas de Gabriel fueron de más a menos. Tal vez los cambios en la industria, tal vez los giros de la vida, o quizás el desgaste natural de los vínculos que no se alimentan con la misma intensidad. Hasta la fecha, no hay reproche por los negocios—porque business is business. Lo que duele es la invisibilidad que se instala con los años, cuando la amistad se vuelve eco y ya no presencia.
Actualizado set. 2025.
textTranslated:
TEXTILES AND VOLCANOES
That day in 2013, Poás Volcano greeted us with its sulfurous breath and its crown of mist. The crater, immense and alive, seemed to breathe with us—a geological pause amidst our own transformations. Beside it, Botos Lagoon slept like a green mirror among giant ferns, a silent witness to encounters that went beyond tourism.

I was accompanied by Gabriel Soler, a Valencian with a quick wit and a restless gaze, a representative of Spanish textile companies such as Eysa Confecciones and Encama. His visit was not by chance: he came in search of new business opportunities, and I, as a textile tradesman with a wealth of experience, offered him my knowledge of the Costa Rican market without charging him a cent. I did so out of a friendship cultivated years before, when Gabriel would arrive at Tienda La Gloria S.A. with his catalogs under his arm and I, as the official buyer, would open the doors of the store to him with the same openness I offered him today to the volcanic landscape.

Amidst jokes, walks, and deep conversations, Gabriel shared with me a concern that already felt like a prophecy: the silent threat posed by China to the Spanish textile industry. He told me about the Valencia trade fairs, the 24,000 square meters of exhibition space, the 3,000 exhibitors showcasing the best of Iberian design… and the thousands of Chinese visitors who came not to negotiate, but to observe, photograph, and copy. Years later, that invisible strategy would plunge one of the world's most refined industries into a crisis of costs, production, and financing that not even the most visionary could have foreseen.

For me, that visit to Poás coincided with another eruption: that of my personal life. In the midst of a divorce, with the grief still fresh, I sought refuge in spiritual retreats that helped me heal and accept. The volcano, with its contained force, seemed to understand me. Gabriel, without fully realizing it, was also part of that process of starting over.

Gabriel's visits became less frequent over time. Perhaps it was due to changes in the industry, perhaps life's twists and turns, or perhaps it was the natural erosion of relationships that weren't nurtured with the same intensity. text:
*Warning*: Be cautious of dishonest parking attendants at Poás Volcano

I recently visited Poás Volcano and parked my car in the designated parking area. When I returned to my vehicle, one of the parking volunteers noticed my tire was flat and kindly offered to change my spare tire. He even refused payment for his help, which initially seemed like a genuine act of kindness. I did tipping him for his help.

Later, when I took my car to a tire shop, I was surprised to find that there was no puncture and the tire was in good condition. It's likely that the parking attendant intentionally let the air out of my tire by opening the valve stem to create an opportunity for a "paid" repair service.

Be cautious when parking at Poás Volcano.

*Rating:* 1/5 stars (parking only)

¡Vaya, qué frustración! Nos sentimos decepcionados cuando llegamos a un lugar como el Volcán Poás y descubrimos que está cerrado sin haber recibido información previa. Este tipo de i

### 1. **Consulta previamente los canales oficiales**
Antes de viajar, revisa la página oficial del Parque Nacional Volcán Poás, redes sociales o contacta directamente a las autoridades locales. Suelen publicar alertas, horarios y cierres de acceso. Así te aseguras de que esté abierto antes de ir.

**Sitios recomendados:**
- Ministerio de Ambiente y Energía de Costa Rica (MINAE)
- Sistema Nacional de Áreas de Conservación (SINAC)
- Redes sociales del parque o del gobierno.

---

### 2. **Reserva con anticipación**
En los últimos años, para visitar lugares turísticos como el Volcán Poás, generalmente se requiere hacer una reserva en línea. Esto te puede dar señales del estado del parque. Si no te permiten reservar o el sistema está inhabilitado, podría ser un indicativo de que está cerrado. Perooooo a nosotros si nos dieron una reserva, solo que después nos la cambiaron.

---

### 3. **Investiga posibles cierres por seguridad**
Dado que el Volcán Poás es activo, hay ocasiones en que la actividad sísmica y volcánica obliga al cierre de sus accesos como medida de seguridad. En ese caso, no hay forma de preverlo con mucha anticipación, pero podrías informarte a través de la Comisión Nacional de Emergencias (CNE) o fuentes locales de noticias.

---

### 4. **Nuestro plan alternativo**

- Catarata La Paz
- Jardín de las Cataratas (La Paz Waterfall Gardens)
- Cefetal  **Doka Estate**
- Laguna de Fraijanes o otros parques cercanos.

Recommendations: Bring a sweater because it's cold; depending on the time of day, wear gloves and a scarf. Entrance fees are purchased online. Parking is now paid for at the cafeteria in cash or by card (2500 colones). Wear hiking boots or non-slip sneakers. Only high-clearance vehicles can reach the top; sedans should be left 150 meters before the summit because the road is in very poor condition. Inside the park, there's a cafeteria with a souvenir shop. Before the entrance booth, on the right, there's an area called La Laguna where you can come by motorcycle, bicycle, or ATV to have fun on the open area. text:
One of the worst experiences I had in Costa Rica! I went here for the first time without a ticket, waited for about an hour in a long car line to enter the national park, only to be turned away. The staff could easily walk through the line every 10-15 minutes to check if people have tickets, saving everyone a lot of time. This place is so popular that it’s often hard to get a ticket for the same day or even the next, so you really need to book your ticket in advance on the SINAC website. There’s no network in the area, so you can’t even check availability once you’re there.

I eventually bought a ticket for $17 ($15 plus taxes) and visited the Poas Volcano a week later. You also need to pay for parking, which costs around $5. Upon arrival, you get a helmet with a color that corresponds to your group. The staff claims it’s for your safety, but in reality, it doesn’t seem necessary. You’ll watch a short video about the volcano and then be allowed to walk to the viewpoint. It’s only a 500-meter walk on an asphalt road, so it’s an easy walk, even in flip-flops.

When you reach the small viewpoint, you only get 20 minutes to view the volcano. I was in the first group at 8 AM, and it was completely foggy, so I couldn’t see anything. I’ve read in reviews that this is common, and many others have the same experience. After 20 minutes, another group arrives with different-colored helmets, and the staff tells you it’s time to leave. There are some hiking routes nearby, but they’re closed, and you’re not allowed to go there. The staff essentially says, “That’s it, your time is up, you need to leave.”

I ended up paying $23 for a short, foggy view of the volcano and basically got nothing out of it. If the volcano is active or there’s a chance of poor visibility, they should just close the place rather than take money for a tiny viewpoint that’s often clouded over. This was a complete waste of time and money. I get that the place is popular since it’s near San José, but it wasn’t worth it in the end.

text:
Es el volcán más alto de Costa Rica a 3432 msnm, las vistas son simplemente increíbles, si es tu primera vez te recomiendo:
- Visitar el sector Volcán Irazu cráteres.
- Explorar y recorrer por completo desde la entrada hasta el final, pasado por el cráter Diego de la Haya, Playa Hermosa y finalmente el cráter principal.
- Luego de esto y salir de la entrads principal del parque avanzado unos 300mts y a la derecha van ver el mirador del volcán, el cual es un lugar EPICO.

Estoy seguro que si lo haces así, el final te dejará impactado, feliz y sabrás que todo el viaje valió completamente la pena.

Update: Antes de ingresar a la entrada del mirador, al otro lado hay un sendero, avanzan un poco y tendrán una vista espectacular del Volcán Turrialba
textTranslated:
It's the highest volcano in Costa Rica at 3,432 meters above sea level. The views are simply incredible. If it's your first time, I recommend:
- Visiting the Irazú Volcano crater area.

- Exploring the entire area from the entrance to the end, passing by the Diego de la Haya crater, Playa Hermosa, and finally the main crater.

- After leaving the main park entrance, walk about 300 meters and you'll see the volcano viewpoint on your right. It's an EPIC spot.

I'm sure that if you do it this way, the end will leave you speechless and happy, and you'll know that the whole trip was completely worth it.

Update: Before entering the viewpoint, there's a trail on the other side. Walk a little further and you'll have a spectacular view of the Turrialba Volcano.

text:
What a beautiful volcano! This is by far the best place I’ve visited that’s managed by SINAC. You need to buy your ticket online in advance, and once you’re there, you’ll have access to two different, wide viewpoints. I left my car parked near the road before entering the park, so I’m not sure about the parking fees.

The first viewpoint is on the highest peak, offering the most stunning view — you can even see the bottom of the caldera. It was a bit cloudy when I visited, but the view was still breathtaking. There were no staff members around, so I was able to fly my drone without any issues. The second viewpoint is larger, but the view isn’t as impressive.

The best part was that you can take as much time as you want to walk around and take photos. No one is there to rush you, unlike at Poas Volcano, which made it much more enjoyable. I was really happy with my experience here!

text:
Hiking the Arenal Volcano was a true bucket-list experience and one I’ll never forget.

The hike is picturesque from start to finish, with stunning views that constantly remind you how powerful and beautiful nature can be. One absolute lifesaver was packing ponchos ahead of time—the weather here is unpredictable and can shift quickly from bright and sunny to overcast and pouring rain in a matter of moments.

I highly recommend hiring a walking tour guide. Having someone explain the rich geological and cultural history of the volcano adds an entirely new layer to the experience. I was genuinely shocked by how much history there is behind Arenal and the surrounding terrain—it transforms the hike from just a scenic walk into an educational journey.

The hike itself offers a solid workout, but it’s well worth the effort. You leave not only physically accomplished, but also with a deeper appreciation for this incredible natural wonder.

The water's coloring phenomenon is a fascinating sight. It's a very popular spot, so it's difficult to find a secluded spot to enjoy a walk through the forest. ⭐ Experiencia inolvidable con Miguel, un guía excepcional

Llegamos al Parque Nacional Volcán Tenorio con la duda de si contratar otro guía, ya que el precio es elevado y ya habíamos tenido otras experiencias previas. Pero encontrar a Miguel en la entrada fue todo un acierto.

Desde el primer momento nos transmitió total confianza y decidimos animarnos. Nos explicó que podíamos elegir entre una ruta de hora y media o alargarla hasta tres horas, todo por el mismo precio. Sin duda, Miguel demostró ser no solo una gran persona, sino un profesional de primera: nos enseñó todo tipo de plantas, animales y detalles que por nuestra cuenta jamás habríamos visto. Su interés por buscarnos cada especie y su pasión por la naturaleza se notan en cada momento.

Al finalizar, tuvo un detalle maravilloso invitándonos a probar piña y fruta de la pasión en la tienda de la entrada, donde además nos explicó las frutas típicas de la zona. Se nota que es una persona querida por todos en el lugar y de esas que realmente vale la pena conocer.

Si visitáis el parque, no dudéis en contactar con él antes. Es un auténtico amante de la naturaleza y los animales. Se lleva nuestro total agradecimiento y recomendación.
textTranslated:
⭐ An unforgettable experience with Miguel, an exceptional guide

We arrived at Tenorio Volcano National Park wondering whether to hire another guide, as the price is high and we'd had previous experiences. But finding Miguel at the entrance was a stroke of luck.

From the very first moment, he inspired complete confidence, and we decided to go for it. He explained that we could choose between a 90-minute tour or extend it to three hours, all for the same price. Without a doubt, Miguel proved to be not only a wonderful person but also a top-notch professional: he showed us all kinds of plants, animals, and details that we would never have noticed on our own. His dedication to finding each species and his passion for nature were evident at every moment.

At the end, he had a wonderful gesture, inviting us to try pineapple and passion fruit at the entrance shop, where he also explained the typical fruits of the area. It's clear that he's a beloved figure in the park and one of those people who is truly worth meeting.

If you visit the park, don't hesitate to contact him beforehand. He is a true nature and animal lover. He has our sincere gratitude and recommendation.

text:
Muy fácil acceso al volcán desde SJ, la carretera impecable y unos vistas hermosas para apreciar mientras manejas. El volcán para Enero 2025 ya no tiene la laguna, así que la vista al cráter no tiene ese toque de color, sin embargo, la planicie de 'playa hermosa' y la vista al valle, si tienes suerte y no está nublado te dará buenas fotos. La cafetería es una tienda de souvenirs donde se paga el parqueo, y se compra café de máquina y un bocadillo. El recorrido puede tomarle unas dos horas con calma.

Compre las entradas en la página del sinac, arriba no hay señal de celular, y es obligatorio entrar con reservación, solo necesita el código de la reserva y su identificación. La entrada cuesta 2$ para  ticos, y 17$ para adulto extranjero.

Use protector solar, lleve sombrero (la gorra no cubre toda su cara) y cubrase el cuerpo del sol. Hace frío y viento, lleve ropa adecuada.

A unos 30 minutos más abajo está Bosque de Prusia, esa caminata es dura, unas dos horas el tramo más corto, puede quedarse haciendo picnic en la entrada del bosque. La entrada se compra aparte en la página del sinac, el parque cierra a las 3:30 pm. También está Sanatorio Durán, recorrerlo con calma le puede tomar otras dos horas.
textTranslated:
Very easy access to the volcano from San José, the road is in excellent condition, and there are beautiful views to enjoy while driving. The volcano will no longer have its lagoon by January 2025, so the view of the crater lacks that vibrant color. However, the "beautiful beach" plain and the valley view, if you're lucky and it's not cloudy, will provide some great photo opportunities. The cafeteria is a souvenir shop where you pay for parking and buy machine-made coffee and a snack. The tour can take about two hours at a leisurely pace.

Purchase tickets on the SINAC website. There's no cell phone signal at the top, and reservations are required. You'll only need the reservation code and your ID. The entrance fee is $2 for Costa Ricans and $17 for foreign adults.

Use sunscreen, wear a hat (a cap won't cover your entire face), and protect yourself from the sun. It's cold and windy, so dress appropriately.

About 30 minutes further down is Prussian Forest. That hike is strenuous, taking about two hours for the shortest section. You can have a picnic at the forest entrance. Entrance fees are purchased separately on the SINAC website. The park closes at 3:30 pm. Sanatorio Durán is also nearby; exploring it at a leisurely pace can take another two hours.

🇩🇪
Heute Morgen sind wir ganz früh mit dem Bus zu einem nahegelegenen Vulkan gefahren. Nach einer etwa zweistündigen Fahrt erreichten wir den Kraterrand. Dort oben, auf einer Höhe von 3.340 Metern, war es eisig kalt. 🌬️❄️ Dichter Nebel hüllte die Landschaft ein, und es hatte zuvor heftig geregnet, sodass der Asphalt der Straße noch dampfte. 🌧️🚐 Ich hatte alle meine Kleidungsschichten an, doch die Kälte drang trotzdem durch. Aber der frische Wind und der beeindruckende Blick auf den Vulkankrater entschädigten für alles. 🌋😊
Nach zweieinhalb Stunden Wanderung kam die Sonne schließlich ein wenig hervor und tauchte alles in ein goldenes Licht. ☀️✨ Mit dem gleichen Bus ging es dann zurück in die Stadt – erschöpft, aber glücklich. ❤️

🇬🇧
This morning, we set off very early by bus to visit a nearby volcano. After about two hours, we reached the crater’s edge. At an altitude of 3,340 meters, it was freezing cold. 🌬️❄️ Thick fog blanketed the area, and it had rained heavily earlier, leaving the asphalt steaming. 🌧️🚐 I wore every layer of clothing I had with me, yet the chill still seeped through. However, the fresh wind and the breathtaking view of the volcanic crater made up for the cold. 🌋😊
After a two-and-a-half-hour hike, the sun finally broke through, casting everything in a warm, golden glow. ☀️✨ We returned to the city on the same bus, tired but happy. ❤️

Το μονοπάτι είναι αρκετά εύκολο και το μόνο λιγάκι πιο δύσκολο σημείο είναι το κατέβασμα και κυρίως το ανέβασμα για τον καταρράκτη. Αξίζει με χίλια να το επισκεφτείτε.

The path is quite easy and the only slightly more difficult point is the descent and mainly the ascent to the waterfall. It is worth a thousand to visit.

text:
We visited Río Celeste, located within Tenorio Volcano National Park. As usual, you need to purchase tickets in advance. A helpful tip is to go early in the morning when there are fewer people.

The park is well-maintained, with a trail that runs through it. Along the way, you can spot a variety of wildlife (snakes, monkeys, sloths, etc.). The trail is fairly easy at the beginning and becomes less developed further in, but it’s not difficult. Eventually, you’ll reach the river and follow it along the side. Its color is absolutely stunning, and the spot where it changes color (due to minerals) is fascinating to see.

It’s a highly recommended visit!

text: El Parque Nacional Volcán Tenorio es un lugar impresionante, especialmente por el increíble río Celeste y su majestuosa catarata. El paisaje es realmente espectacular y vale la pena la visita. Sin embargo, hay que tener en cuenta que el tiempo es imprevisible; durante nuestra visita nos cayó una tormenta, lo que impidió que pudiéramos ver animales. A pesar de esto, disfrutamos mucho del parque. Además, el aparcamiento vigilado en el exterior cuesta 2.000 colones, lo cual nos pareció razonable. Definitivamente, es un lugar que merece la pena explorar.
textTranslated: Tenorio Volcano National Park is a breathtaking place, especially because of the incredible Celeste River and its majestic waterfall. The scenery is truly spectacular and well worth a visit. However, it's important to keep in mind that the weather is unpredictable; during our visit, we were caught in a storm, which prevented us from seeing any wildlife. Despite this, we thoroughly enjoyed the park. Furthermore, the secure parking outside the park costs 2,000 colones, which we found reasonable. It's definitely a place worth exploring.

text:
Años anteriores se podía ver el cráter inundado con ese precioso color. Ahora está seco desde donde la vista llega a alcanzar y solo puedes obtener fotos del cráter ''vacío'' y todo ese maravilloso espacio abierto.

Las vallas en algunas partes están caídas o sustituidas por otras menos costosas (y sin curar) que rompen la estética, precisamente de toda esa extensa limitación.

La cafetería souvenir deja mucho que desear con esas empanadas y enchiladas de patata que no recomiendo. El café está mejor.

Algo para abrigarse y un paraguas nunca estarían de más en esos 3.300 metros de altura. Nunca se sabe.
textTranslated:
In previous years, the crater could be seen flooded with that beautiful color. Now it's dry as far as the eye can see, and you can only get photos of the "empty" crater and all that wonderful open space.

The fences in some places are down or replaced with cheaper (and untreated) ones that ruin the aesthetic, precisely because of all that extensive enclosure.

The souvenir café leaves much to be desired with those potato empanadas and enchiladas, which I don't recommend. The coffee is better.

Something warm and an umbrella would never hurt at that altitude of 3,300 meters. You never know.

text: Solo se puede llegar en barco a Tortuguero. Normalmente desde la Pavona pero también desde San Francisco. El parqueo 10000 colones dos noches y el barco 8000 por persona ida y vuelta. Además hay que pagar la entrada al parque a través de la web SINAC dos meses antes y anotar el número de pase que te dan y te pedirán en la entrada. Esta entrada te permite gozar mediante otro pago según la agencia de cualquier excursión por agua (kayak, canoa o barca motor) o al sendero del jaguar (caminando sin guía para ver monos, lagartijas y pájaros o ver algo más con guía). En agosto te obligaran a ir con botas 2000 colonos más porque en el primer tramo el agua llega más arriba del tobillo. Por la noche, el tour nocturno utiliza ese sendero pero te cobra otra entrada de 7 dolares y te llevan por otro camino hasta el trozo donde casualmente ya no necesitas botas; verás por turnos de grupos a una tortuga poner los huevos, para no estresarla solo se ce ese momento, cuando tapa los huevos, hace otro nido de despiste y se va. La playa es peligrosa para bañarse por las corrientes.
textTranslated: Tortuguero is only accessible by boat. Boats usually depart from La Pavona, but also from San Francisco. Parking costs 10,000 colones for two nights, and the boat fare is 8,000 colones per person round trip. You also need to pay the park entrance fee through the SINAC website two months in advance and note the pass number they give you, which they will ask for at the entrance. This pass allows you to enjoy, for an additional fee depending on the agency, any water excursion (kayaking, canoeing, or motorboat) or the Jaguar Trail (walking without a guide to see monkeys, lizards, and birds, or with a guide for a more extensive tour). In August, they require you to wear boots for an additional 2,000 colones because the water in the first section is above ankle height. At night, the night tour uses this trail but charges a separate fee of $7 and takes you along a different path to the section where, coincidentally, you no longer need boots. You'll see groups of turtles laying their eggs in turns. To avoid stressing them, you only observe them at that moment. Once they've covered their eggs, they'll build another nest as a distraction and leave. The beach is dangerous for swimming due to the currents.

text: We did the Jaguar Trail and liked it (rent water boots if it rained before!) BUT considering the high entrance fee of almost 20 USD incl. taxes for a self-guided hike I really expect SINAC to take better care of the beach. There was stranded trash everywhere and it did clearly not look it was from recent floods. There is also trash at several beach access points in the park which looks like it was collected on the beach by tourists but it's not being disposed by the park staff. If you charge big money please invest part of it in the conversation of the area, especially for the nesting sea turtles. I also saw other parts of the beach where they dump many tourists every night to watch the nesting, everyone paying the NP fees and mandatory guides. Turtles have to crawl over piles of trash to get to their nesting areas, I saw the turtle tracks across the trash. It's awful and sad! Protect what pays your bills if you're not already motivated to protect those creatures.

ATTENTION, Le vrai volcan Irazu en janvier 2023 n'a PAS D'EAU. Cela fait même un certain temps: il est complétement à sec.
Il faut faut donc abaisser ses attentes. Le volcan ressemble davantage à une mine ou une carrière abandonnée, ce qui peut causer une déception de votre visite au Costa Rica.

Notre agence de voyage CAA Québec ne mentionnait pas ce fait, alors la visite est donc moins wow ! D'ailleurs, toutes les photos du volcan Irazu avec de l'eau dans le fond devraient comporter une mise en garde car ce sont des photos non actuelles ou des photos-montages, toute recherche avec un moteur de recherche conduit actuellement à des images différentes de la réalité.

Il n'y a pas de belvèdère aménagé sur le site pour au moins voir le bassin complet, les gens doivent grimper périlleusement sur les clotures pour voir le creux du volcan. Un minimum d'effort des gestionnaires permettrait facilement de dresser une telle installation. Pas de guide, pas d'information...

Marcher sur le plateau de sable/pouissière volcanique est assez intéressant. Est-ce qu'un détour de 3 heures vaut la peine ?
textTranslated:
WARNING: The real Irazu volcano in January 2023 has NO WATER. In fact, it hasn't been for some time: it's completely dry.

So, lower your expectations. The volcano looks more like an abandoned mine or quarry, which could be a disappointment for your Costa Rica trip.

Our travel agency, CAA Québec, didn't mention this fact, so the visit was less impressive! Furthermore, all photos of the Irazu volcano with water at the bottom should include a disclaimer because they are either outdated or photoshopped; any search using a search engine currently leads to images that are different from reality.

There is no viewing platform on the site to even see the entire basin; people have to climb precariously onto the fences to see the volcano's crater. A little effort from the management would easily allow them to build such a structure. No guide, no information...

Walking across the volcanic sand/dust plateau is quite interesting. Is a 3-hour detour worth it?
title: Irazú Volcano

textTranslated: The natural beauty of the entire Tenorio Volcano National Park is astonishing. The Celeste River and the majesty of the waterfall fascinated me. Attractions like the Teñideros Lagoon are impressive, reflecting the wonders of nature. The surrounding tropical forest; the waterfall; the viewpoint with views of the Tenorio Volcano; the Blue Lagoon; the Borbollones; The origin of the Celeste River comes from the union of the Quebrada Agria River and the Buena Vista River. These are excellent places in this beautiful place. There is a place called El Teñideros, where its tributaries converge and the water can be observed in shades ranging from aquamarine, light blue, turquoise, to deep blue. What can I say about the hot springs and all the animals that can be observed there, such as white-tailed deer and birds? The natural attractions of the park are impressive; however, the hike is not extensive, it is 2.5 km, but the trail is not more accessible. Like any trail, it has its challenges, so you have to be prepared, but the experience is excellent. And what can we say about the viewpoint where you can see the Tenorio Volcano? It's a beautiful place worth appreciating. Without a doubt, it's one of the most beautiful natural wonders in the world.

Un bosque primario y nuboso a gran altura. Hay varias rutas que se pueden hacer y están muy bien señalizadas y delimitadas para ir a Río Celeste, Los Teñideros o los borbollones o al mirador.
Las vistas desde el mirador son mágicas.
La subida no es difícil, se tardan unas 2 horas en hacer las rutas, dependiendo del ritmo de cada uno.
El bosque es realmente hermoso, es un bosque húmedo con mucha flora y fauna. Me encantaron las nubes que bajan en el bosque, que le da un toque Místico, el sentimiento de regresar a los orígenes y a lo natural. La naturaleza que tanto nos da, tanta belleza!
Al llegar a Río Celeste o los Teñideros veréis que el agua es de color azul turquesa por la composición química de esta.
En la zona de los borbollones se sentía un olor peculiar debido a la eliberacion de los gases y se podía ver un burbujeo en el agua.
Es un lugar hermoso que merece la pena visitar en CR.
textTranslated:
A high-altitude, primary cloud forest. There are several well-marked and clearly defined trails leading to Río Celeste, Los Teñideros, the bubbling springs, or the viewpoint.

The views from the viewpoint are magical.
The hike isn't difficult; it takes about two hours to complete the trails, depending on your pace.
The forest is truly beautiful, a humid forest teeming with flora and fauna. I loved the clouds descending through the forest, which lend it a mystical touch, a feeling of returning to our origins and to nature. Nature gives us so much, so much beauty!
Upon arriving at Río Celeste or Los Teñideros, you'll see that the water is turquoise blue due to its chemical composition.
In the bubbling springs area, there was a peculiar smell due to the release of gases, and you could see bubbles forming in the water.
It's a beautiful place that's well worth visiting in Costa Rica.

text:
A cerca de duas horas de viagem de La Fortuna, está localizado o Parque Nacional Vulcão Tenorio, que abriga um dos tesouros naturais mais procurados e populares da Costa Rica: o Rio Celeste. Suas águas extremamente azuis ficam encantadoras nas fotos, mesmo debaixo da tradicional chuva costa-riquenha. Para chegar até lá, você pode dirigir um veículo alugado ou contratar um tour, que já inclui guia pela trilha e almoço.

Mas os preços dos passeios são salgados, ficando na casa dos US$ 80 por pessoa. Uma vez no parque, é preciso percorrer uma trilha de seis quilômetros não muito regular – especialmente quando chove – para chegar até a cachoeira, que é o ponto alto do Rio Celeste. São cerca de três horas de caminhada. A entrada no parque custa US$ 12 e pode ser feita das 8h às 16h. O estacionamento custa US$ 4.
textTranslated:
About two hours' drive from La Fortuna lies Tenorio Volcano National Park, home to one of Costa Rica's most sought-after and popular natural treasures: the Rio Celeste. Its intensely blue waters look enchanting in photos, even under the traditional Costa Rican rain. To get there, you can drive a rental car or hire a tour, which includes a guided trail and lunch.

However, tour prices are steep, around US$80 per person. Once in the park, you must hike a six-kilometer trail that is not very regular – especially when it rains – to reach the waterfall, which is the highlight of the Rio Celeste. The hike takes about three hours. Park entrance costs US$12 and is open from 8 am to 4 pm. Parking costs US$4.

text:
Visiting the Arenal Volcano with friends was an unforgettable adventure that combined the raw beauty of nature with thrilling experiences. Nestled in the lush rainforests of Costa Rica, Arenal Volcano stands majestically, offering breathtaking views that captivate from every angle.

As we embarked on guided hikes around the volcano, we were enveloped by the vibrant flora and fauna. The trails were well-maintained and offered varying levels of difficulty, accommodating both casual walkers and avid hikers. Our guide was knowledgeable, sharing fascinating insights about the ecosystem and the volcano’s history.

One of the highlights was the natural hot springs, a perfect way to unwind after a day of trekking. We soaked in the mineral-rich waters, surrounded by the sounds of the rainforest — a truly serene experience that felt like a slice of paradise.

For those seeking an adrenaline rush, the zip-lining experience through the treetops provided an exhilarating perspective of the area. Flying over the canopy with the imposing Arenal in the background was both thrilling and awe-inspiring.

Throughout our stay, the local hospitality was exceptional. We indulged in delicious Costa Rican cuisine and enjoyed the vibrant culture and warmth of the local people.

Arenal Volcano is a destination that thrills, relaxes, and educates, making it a must-visit for nature lovers and adventure seekers alike. This journey with friends will be cherished for a lifetime, and we left with memories etched in our hearts and a deeper appreciation for the wonders of Costa Rica.

text:
Vanuit Tortuguero zijn er 2 opties:
- tour met bootjes (te huren bij verblijf of op locatie). Let wel op, als je zelf wil roeien dan ga je best voor de kayak tour. De cano tour is met een iets grotere boot en de gids roeit.
- jaguar trail (te boeken aan ingang en kan zonder gids).

De boottochten zijn oké, veel uitleg, vogels,… Ook uitleg over Tortuguero zelf. Maar je bent zeker niet alleen op het water, veel andere boten met toeristen.

De Jaguar trail is 6 km in totaal en je wandelt dezelfde route heen als terug of via het strand. Wij hebben dit alleen gedaan, maar met een gids is dit dezelfde route. Apen van op korte afstand kunnen bekijken, luiaard… Een jaguar zal je zeker niet zien.

De andere parken in Costa Rica zullen vermoedelijk meer te bieden hebben (avontuurlijk gezien).
Indien je eerst de andere kant van Costa Rica hebt gedaan, zou ik nadien niet meer naar Tortuguero gaan.
1 tot 2 dagen is zeker voldoende om alles gezien te hebben. Al ben je misschien teleurgesteld als je de rest eerst deed.
textTranslated:
From Tortuguero, there are two options:
- Boat tours (available for rent at your accommodation or on-site). Note that if you want to row yourself, it's best to choose the kayak tour. The canoe tour uses a slightly larger boat, and the guide rows.
- Jaguar Trail (bookable at the entrance and available without a guide).

The boat trips are okay, with plenty of explanation, birdlife, and more. There's also information about Tortuguero itself. But you're certainly not alone on the water; there are many other boats with tourists.

The Jaguar Trail is 6 km in total, and you walk the same route there and back, or along the beach. We did this solo, but with a guide, it's the same route. You can spot monkeys up close, sloths, and more. You definitely won't see a jaguar.

The other parks in Costa Rica will likely have more to offer (adventure-wise).
If you've already explored the other side of Costa Rica, I wouldn't go back to Tortuguero. One to two days is definitely enough to see everything. Although you might be disappointed if you did the rest first.

address: Limón Province, Roxana, Costa Rica

text: Für uns war der Besuch des NP eines der schönsten Erlebnisse in Costa Rica auch wenn es kleine Abstriche gibt. Beginnen wir mit der Anreise: ist gut über viele kleine Straßen erreichbar, der Parkplatz war ok und scheint überwacht zu sein - die Tagesgebühr für 20 US$ ist viel zu hoch und hier wird einfach nur ausgenutzt, dass es keine andere Alternative gibt. Die Fahrt mit dem Boot (ca. 1h) kostet pro Person und Fahrt 15 US$ - hier muss man sagen, dass sich die fahrt wirklich lohnt und man schon die ersten Highlights wie Kaimane, Krokodile sowie Schildkröten sieht. Angekommen im Ort sucht man sich dann die gebuchte Unterkunft und kann nun zwischen verschiedenen geführten Touren wählen oder man erkundet Strand und Umland auf eigene Faust. Alles ist sehr sauber und aufgeräumt, die Leute sind sehr gastfreundlich und es gibt eine breite Auswahl an Restaurants und Shops.
textTranslated: For us, visiting the national park was one of the most beautiful experiences in Costa Rica, even if there were a few minor drawbacks. Let's start with the journey there: it's easily accessible via many small roads, the parking lot was okay and seemed to be monitored – the daily fee of US$20 is far too high and simply exploits the fact that there's no other option. The boat trip (about 1 hour) costs US$15 per person each way – and it has to be said that the trip is really worth it, as you see the first highlights like caimans, crocodiles, and turtles. Once you arrive in town, you find your booked accommodation and can then choose between various guided tours or explore the beach and surrounding area on your own. Everything is very clean and tidy, the people are very hospitable, and there's a wide selection of restaurants and shops.

Die Anfahrt geht über Gelände der Hacienda Guachipelin, deswegen etwas Kleingeld bereithalten. 😉

Wir waren im Anschluss noch beim La Leona Waterfall - eine gute Kombi, wenn man in der Gegend ist.

We hiked in the "Las Pailas" sector. It was a pleasant hike through very dry terrain (in April!), but I had hoped for a bit more variety (the fumaroles and mini-volcanic activity are impressive, but they're quite repetitive on the loop trail). That's really nitpicking, though; the country is simply too beautiful, and we've been spoiled by all our experiences so far. 😃 It was a bit annoying that some of the signs pointed in the wrong direction. Our highlight was the not-so-safe and unexpected encounter with a tapir (it was right in front of us)! They're not actually typical for this area.

The access road goes through the grounds of Hacienda Guachipelin, so have some small change ready. 😉

Afterwards, we visited La Leona Waterfall – a great combination if you're in the area.

Un nome:ABEL, il Tarzan del Tortuguero.
È una guida bravissima che ci ha accompagnati in una camminata di due ore nel parco. Parla perfettamente inglese e spagnolo ma sa qualche parola in qualsiasi lingua. È un genio della comunicazione ;-)
Lui PARLA CON GLI ANIMALI! Sa imitare i versi di tantissimi volatili e rane. È incredibile, gli animali si fermano e lo cercano sentendone il richiamo.

In soli 5 km di camminata abbiamo potuto ammirare tucani, rane, scimmie urlatrici, scimmie cappuccino, serpenti, iguana, FORMICHIERE, volatili vari, geki…e tanti altri.

Senza di lui avremmo visto solo le tipiche scimmie, che sono comunque stupende.

Abbiamo fatto anche il canoe tour al mattino presto, che merita.

Ci ricorderemo questo giorno per sempre !
textTranslated:
A name: ABEL, the Tarzan of Tortuguero.
He's a fantastic guide who took us on a two-hour walk through the park. He speaks perfect English and Spanish, but he knows a few words in every language. He's a communication genius ;-)
He TALKS TO ANIMALS! He can imitate the sounds of countless birds and frogs. It's incredible; the animals stop and look for him when they hear his call.

In just a 5-km walk, we were able to admire toucans, frogs, howler monkeys, capuchin monkeys, snakes, iguanas, anteaters, various birds, geckos... and many others.

Without him, we would have only seen the typical monkeys, which are still beautiful.

We also took the early morning canoe tour, which was worth it.

We will remember this day forever!

Highly recommended — truly unforgettable.

text:
Wir hatten Mitte Oktober leider Pech mit dem Wetter und es hat jeden Tag sehr lange geregnet. Die Schildkröten könnten wir daher beim schlüpfen leider nicht sehen. Man könnte allerdings morgens immer einige Spuren sehen, sodass nachts auf jeden Fall einiges los war.
Mit einer Tour haben wir auch nachts die Eiablage in Teilen sehen können.
Den Eintritt für den Jaguar trail haben wir uns mit 17 Dollar gespart. Insgesamt ist die Anreise mit Auto und Boot über Pavona Recht lang, das Boot ist jeweils 1h45 pro Weg gefahren und die Fahrt war nicht so angenehm durch den Regen. Wenn man unbedingt Schildkröten sehen möchte, sollte man herkommen, ansonsten kann man auch super als alternative in den Corcovado Nationalpark oder einen einfacher erreichbaren Ort der Karibikseite.
textTranslated:
Unfortunately, we had bad luck with the weather in mid-October, and it rained very heavily every day. As a result, we couldn't see the turtles hatching. However, we could always see some signs in the mornings, so there was definitely a lot of activity at night.

We were able to see parts of the egg-laying at night on a guided tour.

We saved ourselves the $17 entrance fee for the Jaguar Trail. Overall, the journey by car and boat via Pavona is quite long; the boat trip took 1 hour and 45 minutes each way, and the rain made the ride rather unpleasant. If you absolutely want to see turtles, you should come here; otherwise, Corcovado National Park or an easier-to-reach location on the Caribbean coast are excellent alternatives.

text: Schon die Anreise nach Tortuguero – die ausschließlich per Boot möglich is, bildet den ersten Teil des Abenteuers und führt durch traumhafte Kanallandschaften. Der Ort selbst ist das lebendige Zentrum des Nationalparks. Er hat sich über die Jahre zu einem bedeutenden touristischen Knotenpunkt entwickelt, was die Infrastruktur verbessert und viele Reisende anzieht. Die wachsende Beliebtheit ermöglicht es der lokalen Gemeinschaft, sich für den Schutz der Natur und der Schildkröten einzusetzen. Die Erkundung der Wasserstraßen ist ein absolutes Highlight! Die ruhigen Bootsausflüge durch das verzweigte Kanalsystem sind eine fantastische Möglichkeit, tief in den Dschungel vorzudringen. ​Die nächtliche Schildkröten Tour zur Beobachtung der Eiablage ist ein langatmiges Naturschauspiel und der Hauptgrund für viele Besucher. Der Guide sorgt dafür, dass man trotz vieler Gruppen diesem Prozess respektvoll beiwohnen kann. Aufgrund der späten Nachtstunden und der erforderlichen Geduld ist diese Tour für kleinere Kinder möglicherweise nicht ideal. Das Beobachten eines so komplexen Naturvorgangs erfordert Zeit und Geduld. Die gesamte Prozedur kann sich über eineinhalb bis zwei Stunden erstrecken.
textTranslated: Even the journey to Tortuguero – accessible only by boat – forms the first part of the adventure, leading through breathtaking canal landscapes. The town itself is the vibrant heart of the national park. Over the years, it has developed into a significant tourist hub, improving infrastructure and attracting many visitors. This growing popularity allows the local community to dedicate itself to the protection of nature and the turtles. Exploring the waterways is an absolute highlight! The tranquil boat trips through the intricate canal system offer a fantastic way to delve deep into the jungle. The nighttime turtle egg-laying tour is a lengthy natural spectacle and the main draw for many visitors. The guide ensures that, despite the large number of groups, everyone can observe this process respectfully. Due to the late hour and the required patience, this tour may not be ideal for young children. Observing such a complex natural process demands time and patience. The entire procedure can take between one and a half and two hours.

Costa Rica is becoming a victim of its own success… frankly, avoid it: to see volcanoes, go elsewhere… to Iceland, for example, and save $16 for your next trip. ​Der Nationalpark Tortuguero ist ein absolutes Highlight und ein unvergessliches Naturerlebnis! Wir waren überwältigt von der Vielfalt der Tierwelt, die wir dort hautnah erleben durften.
​Wir haben viele Tiere und Schlangen gesehen – darunter Affen, verschiedene Schlangen und andere Reptilien. Das absolute Highlight war aber, als wir eine geschlüpfte Baby-Schildkröte auf ihrem Weg zum Meer beobachten konnten – ein magischer Moment! Die Natur ist hier einfach spektakulär.
​Allerdings möchte ich dringend einen Guide empfehlen. Ohne die Hilfe eines erfahrenen Führers hätten wir die meisten dieser Tiere und die Schildkröte wahrscheinlich verpasst. Der Guide wusste genau, wo man suchen musste und hat uns viele faszinierende Informationen gegeben. Die Investition hat sich absolut gelohnt und das Erlebnis perfekt gemacht!
​5 von 5 Sternen – Ein Muss für jeden, der die einzigartige Tierwelt Costa Ricas erleben möchte.
textTranslated:
A dreamlike natural paradise in Tortuguero National Park!

Tortuguero National Park is an absolute highlight and an unforgettable nature experience! We were overwhelmed by the diversity of wildlife that we were able to experience up close.

We saw many animals and snakes – including monkeys, various snakes, and other reptiles. The absolute highlight, however, was when we were able to observe a hatched baby turtle on its way to the sea – a truly magical moment! Nature here is simply spectacular.

However, I would strongly recommend hiring a guide. Without the help of an experienced guide, we would probably have missed most of these animals and the turtle. The guide knew exactly where to look and gave us a wealth of fascinating information. The investment was absolutely worthwhile and made the experience perfect!

5 out of 5 stars – A must for anyone who wants to experience the unique wildlife of Costa Rica.

Against my better judgement I accepted the rental even without an auto shutoff wristband so the jet ski continued on for 50 yards from where we were dumped by the time it stopped. Do yourself a favor and enjoy the beach but don’t rent from the guys on Playa Conchal until you see that have updated their machines.

text: Conchal Beach is the most beautiful beach we saw in Costa Rica. The sand is broken up sea shells, and the water is turquoise blue. It is a little tricky to get to, though. The best way is to park in the parking lot near the entrance to the town of Brasilito (about $ 6 US for the day). Walk down the street to the waterfront and walk south along the beach. You will see a rock outcropping, and Conchal Beach is on the other side of that. There is a trail cut through the rocks that will get you to the beach. It is about a 20 minute walk from the parking area. Bring water, towels, and if you can, a folding chair. There are vendors on the beach selling drinks or renting a canopy and chairs, but they are pretty expensive.

I wanted this place to be good because I was craving a real Costa Rican meal for me and my family after we swam at Conchal Beach. We stopped here for lunch around 1 p.m. We were the only table there, no other customers. I thought it was because it was early.

We ordered meals for the three of us, and it took them 40 minutes to bring the dishes to the table. The waiter was very kind and attentive, which was the only good thing about the experience. I thought they might be waiting for the cook to arrive or something, but they couldn’t explain why it took so long.

Then they served everyone in my family except me. I had to wait another 10 minutes while watching everyone eat, which made me anxious. We were all starving.

When they finally brought my nachos (yes, just nachos, nothing complicated), they were the worst I’ve ever tried. I ordered them because they are usually easy, fast, and delicious, or at least that has been my experience in the other three restaurants in Costa Rica where I’ve ordered nachos.

The dishes my other family members had were not good either.

text:
Fui a un restaurante en Brasilito y la verdad me llevé una muy buena impresión.

La comida estaba muy, muy rica, con bastante variedad de platos y porciones abundantes — incluso me quedó para llevar y comer después. La chuleta estaba jugosa, bien sazonada y con excelente sabor. Además, los precios me parecieron bastante baratos para la calidad y cantidad que sirven.

Como punto a mejorar, el servicio podría ser un poco más amable; la atención se sintió un poco sin ganas, y eso siempre influye en la experiencia. Sin embargo, fuera de ese detalle, es un muy buen lugar.

Definitivamente recomendado por la comida y los precios.

//

I visited a restaurant in Brasilito and had a very good experience overall.

The food was very, very tasty, with a great variety of dishes and generous portions — I even had leftovers to take home. The pork chop was juicy, well-seasoned, and full of flavor. On top of that, the prices were quite affordable for the quality and portion sizes.

As a small suggestion, the service could be a bit more welcoming; the staff seemed a little unmotivated, which slightly affects the overall experience. Other than that, it’s a very good place.

Definitely recommended for the food and value.

textTranslated:
I went there a few hours ago to eat, and my experience was terrible. The place was in awful condition: the restroom was filthy, the floor was dirty, the tables were dirty, and the fans were very old and worn out.

I ordered a pineapple in water, mixed nachos, an 8,000-colon fish dish, and a michelada. In total, I paid 22,000 colones, which was not reflected in the quality at all.

The nachos were very mediocre, the fish was overly salty, and the milkshake was almost all foam. It was truly a regrettable experience. I absolutely do not recommend it.

text:
First - this is quite a long beach with few access points. We read tge reviews and decided to access the beach at it's southerly point.
There's a reason why so many beachgoers you encounter are pitched under the trees and fronds- the tide really comes in here. This squeezes the sand "pathway" quite a bit so you might think you can stretch out on open sand when you arrive but mid-afternoon, you'll be retreating and realising what local knowledge is worth!!
The waves aren't as high or perhaps as rough, but we tried snorkeling, as some reviews recommend, and you can't see anything. Maybe further up the beach?
But the water is lovely and warm, very swimmable.
There are stones and pebbles underfoot but not too many.
You can hire already pitched gazebos and the restaurant cooked good food off their BBQ.

text: 4/25 si arriva via terra con una semplice macchina a 2 ruote motrici perché la strada è tutta asfaltata. Si raggiunge un parcheggio a pagamento dove poter lasciare l'auto. Ci si imbarca su un battello con una trentina di posti e si naviga sul fiume verso il centro abitato per circa un'oretta. Noi abbiamo trovato un capitano che ci ha fatto fare un safari sul fiume, si fermava appena avvistavamo qualcosa. Iguana, scimmie, caimani e uccelli di tutti i colori. Ci abbiamo impiegato di più ma siamo stati contentissimi. Durante il soggiorno abbiamo fatto un'escursione notturna alla ricerca di fauna tipo, insetti, bradipi, serpenti, ragni. Di giorno invece le escursioni sono in canoa, kayak a piedi o con una barca a motore. Si percorre un tratto di fiume dove poter avvistare uccelli, bradipi, caimani e altre cose interessanti. Consigliatissimo
textTranslated: 4/25 can be reached by land with a simple 2WD vehicle, as the road is entirely paved. You'll reach a paid parking lot where you can leave your car. You'll board a boat with about thirty seats and cruise the river toward the town for about an hour. We found a captain who took us on a river safari, stopping as soon as we spotted something: iguanas, monkeys, caimans, and birds of every color. It took us longer, but we were very happy. During our stay, we took a nighttime excursion in search of wildlife, insects, sloths, snakes, and spiders. During the day, excursions are by canoe, kayak, foot, or motorboat. The tour follows a stretch of river where you can spot birds, sloths, caimans, and other interesting species. Highly recommended.

address: Limón Province, Roxana, Costa Rica
name: Barbara V
text: Che bella Tortuguero. Mi è piaciuta moltissimo a partire dal viaggio per arrivarci con le barche lungo il fiume. Può capitare di vedere i caimani crogiolarsi al sole oppure gli aironi i pappagalli e le scimmie. La mattina siamo andati in kayak all'alba per assistere al risveglio della foresta. Un'esperienza unica. Tortuguero è piccola c'è solo una piccola via dove troverete gli alberghi e i ristoranti. Ma è così pittoresca da rallegrarti il cuore.  Imperdibile il giro della foresta pluviale nella notte. Bellissima!
textTranslated: Tortuguero is beautiful. I loved it, starting with the boat ride along the river. You might see alligators basking in the sun, or herons, parrots, and monkeys. In the morning, we went kayaking at dawn to watch the forest awaken. A unique experience. Tortuguero is small; there's only one narrow road where you'll find the hotels and restaurants. But it's so picturesque it'll warm your heart. The nighttime tour of the rainforest is a must. Beautiful!
title: Parque Nacional Tortuguero

address: Limón Province, Roxana, Costa Rica

text: Tortuguero National Park is an absolutely amazing experience—truly one of a kind in the world. The combination of dense rainforest, winding canals, and the Caribbean coastline creates a unique ecosystem that’s bursting with life. Everywhere you look, there's nature at its finest: monkeys swinging through the trees, colorful toucans flying overhead, and even crocodiles resting by the water. If you're lucky, you might even witness sea turtles nesting on the beach—an unforgettable moment. It’s a place where you feel completely immersed in the wild. A must-visit for any nature lover!

Die Touren erfolgen mit dem Boot sowie auf einigen wenigen Wanderwegen, wobei hier besonders die Nachtwanderungen empfehlenswert sind. text: Dank Guide und einer privaten Familientour konnten wir auf der dreistündigen Tour jede Menge Tiere entdecken. Toucane, Faultiere, Schlangen, kämpfende Waschbären, Frösche, Reptilien, Vögel und Affen. Die Affen waren sogar ganz nah bei uns und turnten durch die Bäume, was auch für die Kinder natürlich ein besonderes Erlebnis war. Wir bekamen ganz viel Hintergrundwissen und konnten jederzeit Fragen stellen. Aufgrund von umgekippten Bäumen war der Weg leider teilweise gesperrt und wir konnten von Puerto Vargas nur bis zum Strand laufen. Mit den Kindern war diese Strecke aber gerade richtig und es gab trotzdem so viel zu entdecken. Unser Guide machte seine Arbeit mit sehr viel Leidenschaft und freute sich sichtlich selbst über jedes Tier, das ihm über den Weg lief. Ein Ausflugsziel, das man an der Karibikküste nicht auslassen sollte!
textTranslated: Thanks to our guide and a private family tour, we were able to spot a huge variety of animals on the three-hour hike. Toucans, sloths, snakes, fighting raccoons, frogs, reptiles, birds, and monkeys. The monkeys were even quite close to us, swinging through the trees, which was a special experience for the children. We learned a lot about the animals and could ask questions at any time. Unfortunately, due to fallen trees, part of the trail was closed, and we could only walk from Puerto Vargas to the beach. However, this distance was just right for the children, and there was still so much to discover. Our guide was incredibly passionate about his work and clearly delighted in every animal he encountered. A must-do excursion on the Caribbean coast!

text: Insgesamt ein sehr schöner Park in dem man viele Tiere sehen kann. Leider haben die Guides die dort Touren anbieten, den Besuch etwas schlechter gemacht. Schon beim Eingang wird man energisch angesprochen, dass man einen Guide buchen soll, da man ansonsten keine Tiere sieht. Wir haben uns dagegen entschieden, weil wir schon lange durch Zentralamerika reisen und einfach einen entspannten Tag verbringen wollten. Man sieht in dem Park viele Tiere (ohne die Hilfe eines Guide). Wir haben Affen, verschiedene Vögel, Leguane, Krebse, Faultiere und Waschbären gesehen. Als wir ein Faultier entdeckten, standen wir in der Nähe einer Gruppe, die einen Guide hatte. Er hat uns dann sehr wütend darauf hingewiesen, dass wir ihn nicht bezahlen und deswegen auch kein Recht hätten ihm zuzuhören. Das ist natürlich in einem Park mir schmalen Wegen und vielen Menschen schwierig. In der Regel finde ich, dass man immer einen Guide beauftragen kann und sollte wenn man möchte, da es für die Leute ihre Möglichkeit ist Geld zu verdienen. So aufdringlich und unangenehm habe ich es aber noch nie erlebt. Leider sind die Guides nur so lange freundlich, wie sie Geld von einem bekommen. Deswegen kann ich in diesem Park nur davon abraten. Die Mitarbeiter des Parks sind aber sehr freundlich und der Eintritt ist auf Spendenbasis, was auch sehr positiv ist.
textTranslated: Overall, a very beautiful park where you can see many animals. Unfortunately, the guides who offer tours there somewhat detracted from the experience. Right at the entrance, you're aggressively pressured to book a guide, as you supposedly won't see any animals otherwise. We decided against it because we've been traveling through Central America for a long time and simply wanted to spend a relaxing day. You can see many animals in the park (without the help of a guide). We saw monkeys, various birds, iguanas, crabs, sloths, and raccoons. When we spotted a sloth, we were standing near a group that had a guide. He then very angrily pointed out that we weren't paying him and therefore had no right to listen to him. This is, of course, difficult in a park with narrow paths and many people. Generally, I think you can and should always hire a guide if you want, as it's their way of earning money. However, I've never experienced such pushy and unpleasant behavior. Unfortunately, the guides are only friendly as long as they're getting money from you. Therefore, I can only advise against visiting this park. However, the park staff are very friendly and the entrance fee is donation-based, which is also a big plus.

address: Alajuela Province, Upala, Costa Rica
name: Cris Nistico
text:
O antigo vulcão Rincón de la Vieja teve sua última erupção em 1983, com uma pequena emissão de cinzas e lava em 1991. A caminhada é de um dia até o topo da cúpula através de uma trilha de seis quilômetros que se origina em Las Pailas.  A jornada ao longo da trilha revelará vários ecossistemas diferentes. Você verá Von Seebach, a principal cratera do vulcão (tem na minha foto), periodicamente solta vapor como evidência de sua atividade geotérmica.
É a caminhada maior do parque. O parque é dividido em caminhadas circulares e o circulo maior, de mais tempo, é para subir ao vulcão de mesmo nome do parque nacional. Vale a pena!
Aqueles que completam a caminhada serão recompensados ​​com paisagens da Península de Nicoyae o Lago da Nicarágua. Se o céu estiver excepcionalmente claro, você poderá ver o Lago Los Jilgueros e quase toda a Costa Rica.
Em mais de 34.000 acres, o parque Rincón de la Vieja tem espaço para dois vulcões, 32 rios e córregos, e uma incrível variedade de flora e fauna.
textTranslated:
The ancient Rincón de la Vieja volcano last erupted in 1983, with a small emission of ash and lava in 1991. The hike is a one-day trek to the summit via a six-kilometer trail that originates in Las Pailas. The journey along the trail will reveal several different ecosystems. You will see Von Seebach, the volcano's main crater (pictured in my photo), periodically release steam as evidence of its geothermal activity.
It is the longest hike in the park. The park is divided into circular hikes, and the longest, larger circle hike is to climb the volcano of the same name as the national park. It's worth it!
Those who complete the hike will be rewarded with views of the Nicoya Peninsula and Lake Nicaragua. If the sky is exceptionally clear, you may be able to see Lake Los Jilgueros and almost all of Costa Rica.

Spanning over 34,000 acres, Rincón de la Vieja National Park boasts two volcanoes, 32 rivers and streams, and an incredible array of flora and fauna.

text:
La compra del ticket de entrada se hace en el lugar, muy rápido, se puede pagar en efectivo o tarjeta... Amplio parqueo y parqueo para autos de personas con discapacidad... Bastantes senderos donde se pueden ver bastantes animales como perezosos, mapaches, serpientes, etc... Se puede acceder a Playa Vargas... Se puede ingresar alimentos no preparados (tipo snacks), bebidas (no alcohólicas)... El lugar en si, es muy bonito, hay mucho para disfrutar, ver y hacer... Es recomendable llegar desde temprano para poder disfrutar de todo lo que ofrece... El sendero a Puerto Vargas es de 2.5km y está preparado para que una persona que ocupa silla de ruedas, pueda recorrerlo sin problema hasta la misma playa, lo que lo hace un parque nacional apto para todos.

Fue una visita muy agradable.

Le damos 9.8/10 pandapuntos

Pandaventuras 🌿🐼🌿
textTranslated:
The entrance ticket is purchased on-site, very quickly, and can be paid for with cash or card. There's ample parking and parking for people with disabilities. Several trails offer opportunities to see various animals such as sloths, raccoons, snakes, and more. You can also access Vargas Beach. You're allowed to bring in unprepared food (like snacks) and non-alcoholic beverages. The park itself is beautiful, with much to enjoy, see, and do. It's recommended to arrive early to fully enjoy everything it has to offer. The trail to Puerto Vargas is 2.5 km long and is wheelchair accessible, allowing people to easily travel all the way to the beach, making it a national park suitable for everyone.

It was a very pleasant visit.

We give it 9.8/10 panda points.

text:
Sin duda, el mejor parque que visitamos en Costa Rica y el lugar donde más fauna pudimos observar. Vimos perezosos, monos carablanca, serpientes, aves de todo tipo y mucha más biodiversidad. Además, la playa es espectacular, de las más bonitas que vimos durante el viaje.

El parque tiene dos accesos. Nosotros entramos por la entrada gestionada por voluntarios, donde la aportación es voluntaria (aunque recomiendan unos 5-6 dólares). La otra entrada tiene un precio fijo similar y dispone de aparcamiento gratuito. En la entrada de los voluntarios no hay parking y algunas personas intentan convencerte de pagar por aparcar, diciendo que al coche le puede pasar algo. Nosotros lo dejamos en la calle y no tuvimos ningún problema.

Tampoco creemos que sea necesario contratar un guía. Son bastante insistentes al ofrecer el servicio, pero recorriendo el sendero por libre, caminando despacio y en silencio, se ven muchísimos animales, ya que la propia gente se va avisando cuando encuentra alguno.

Como aspecto a mejorar, creemos que el parque debería ser más accesible. Nos habían comentado que estaba adaptado, pero la realidad es que solo un tramo de unos dos kilómetros cuenta con pasarelas de madera. El recorrido completo es de unos nueve kilómetros y, con la marea alta, tuvimos que caminar por el agua, pasar por zonas de piedras y hasta saltar troncos caídos. Sería fantástico ampliar las pasarelas para que personas con movilidad reducida, lesiones o familias con carritos pudieran disfrutar de una mayor parte del recorrido.

También nos llamó la atención el control de acceso: revisan las mochilas y no permiten entrar comida ni plásticos, algo que nos parece una buena medida para proteger la fauna. Sin embargo, una vez dentro vimos varias personas con neveras y comida en la playa, por lo que la norma no parece aplicarse de la misma manera a todo el mundo.

Aun con estos detalles, la experiencia fue increíble. Es un parque precioso, muy bien conservado y, para nosotros, el mejor lugar de Costa Rica para disfrutar de la naturaleza y observar animales en libertad. Una visita totalmente imprescindible.
textTranslated:
Without a doubt, the best park we visited in Costa Rica and the place where we saw the most wildlife. We saw sloths, white-faced capuchin monkeys, snakes, all kinds of birds, and much more biodiversity. The beach is also spectacular, one of the most beautiful we saw during the trip.

The park has two entrances. We entered through the entrance managed by volunteers, where the donation is voluntary (although they recommend around $5-6). The other entrance has a similar fixed price and offers free parking. There's no parking at the volunteer entrance, and some people try to convince you to pay to park, saying something might happen to your car. We left ours on the street and had no problems.

We also don't think it's necessary to hire a guide. They're quite insistent on offering the service, but by walking the trail on your own, slowly and quietly, you see many animals, as people alert each other when they spot one.

As an area for improvement, we think the park should be more accessible. We had been told it was accessible, but the reality is that only a two-kilometer stretch has wooden walkways. The entire route is about nine kilometers long, and at high tide, we had to wade through the water, cross rocky areas, and even jump over fallen logs. It would be fantastic to extend the walkways so that people with reduced mobility, injuries, or families with strollers could enjoy a larger portion of the trail.

We were also struck by the access control: they check backpacks and don't allow food or plastic, which we think is a good measure to protect the wildlife. However, once inside, we saw several people with coolers and food on the beach, so the rule doesn't seem to be applied equally to everyone.

Even with these minor issues, the experience was incredible. It's a beautiful park, very well maintained, and, for us, the best place in Costa Rica to enjoy nature and observe animals in their natural habitat. A truly essential visit.

text: Wir waren ein wenig skeptisch, den Nationalpark Tortuguero zu besuchen, da dieser auf allen Reiseprogrammen steht und deswegen auf uns wie eine Touristenfalle wirkte. Doch wir wurden positiv überrascht. Der Besuch lohnt sich auf alle Fälle. Schon rein die Anfahrt mit dem Schiff ist ein schönes Abenteuer für sich. Empfehlenswert ist natürlich eine Bootstour, denn auf dieser sieht man viele verschiedene Tiere und kann deren Geräuschen und Lauten hören. Die Leguane z.B. befanden sich in der Paarungszeit. Daher waren die Männchen orange gefärbt statt wie sonst üblich grünlich. Zum Abschluss der Bootstour besuchten wir noch den Strand in Tortuguero und mit etwas Glück, findet man auch kleine Schildkröten schlüpfen. Zu einer anderen Jahreszeit – wir waren Mitte November da -, dürften vermutlich die grossen, eiablegende Schildkörten zu sehen sein.
textTranslated: We were a little skeptical about visiting Tortuguero National Park, as it's on every travel itinerary and therefore seemed like a tourist trap. But we were pleasantly surprised. It's definitely worth a visit. The boat trip alone is a wonderful adventure. A boat tour is highly recommended, as you can see many different animals and hear their sounds. The iguanas, for example, were in their mating season. Therefore, the males were orange instead of their usual greenish color. To conclude our boat tour, we visited the beach in Tortuguero, and with a bit of luck, you might even see baby turtles hatching. At a different time of year – we were there in mid-November – you'd probably see the large, egg-laying turtles.

text:
Tortuguero National Park covers a coastal area in the Limón region. The best way to reach the park is to go to the El Embarcadero La Pavona and, from there, take a boat to the village of Tortuguero. If you’re staying in the park, they will recommend companies that provide this service.
One of the park’s main attractions is witnessing the turtle nesting (it’s important to ensure you’re visiting during the nesting season). The process is set up to be minimally intrusive to the turtles. Tourists visit in groups, with a guide, to a specific area of the beach. Nothing that emits light is allowed, not even a smartwatch, to protect the turtle nesting process. Each group is assigned to a different zone. Meanwhile, trackers move along the beach in the dark, looking for turtles coming ashore to lay their eggs. When one is found, a group of tourists can approach. They can only see the last part of the nesting (the actual laying of eggs, when the turtle hides them, and when she returns to the sea).
Besides this activity, it’s also worth taking a tour through the canals or walking along the Jaguar Trail.

Wir haben auch ohne Guide viele Tiere gesehen (Affen, Schlange, Waschbären, Schmetterlinge, kleine Salamander). Da wir schon sehr viel gelaufen sind in diesem Urlaub, haben wir nach 2 km umgedreht und waren danach noch schnorcheln (nur mit Anbieter, wird am Eingang angeboten). Entry is donation-based, and your backpack is searched at the entrance (no plastic, no alcohol, no snorkeling equipment, etc.). We saw lots of animals even without a guide (monkeys, snakes, raccoons, butterflies, and small salamanders). Since we'd already done a lot of walking on this trip, we turned around after 2 km and went snorkeling (only with a tour operator, offered at the entrance). That was great too; we saw lots of fish and even three sharks, although the visibility wasn't great.

text: Hermoso parque fuimos x el día desde San José, la ruta son casi 4 hrs así que debes salir muy muy temprano (4:30 - 05.00am) desde San José debes llegar a embarcadero la Pavona ahí puedes dejar tu auto x 10 usd el día , luego tomar una embarcación que también cobra y que te lleva hasta el pueblo Tortuguero , desde ahí puedes tomar algún tours hacia dentro del parque nacional para el cual obvio debes pagar y además comprar el ticket de entrada al parque a través de la Pag del Sinac, recomiendo tomar un tours con algún guía local, nosotros tomamos tours en canoa con don Feliciano ! textTranslated: Beautiful park! We went for the day from San José. The route is almost 4 hours, so you have to leave very, very early (4:30 - 5:00 am). From San José, you need to get to the La Pavona dock. There you can leave your car for $10 USD for the day, then take a boat (also a paid service) that takes you to the village of Tortuguero. From there, you can take a tour into the national park, for which you obviously have to pay, and you also have to buy your park entrance ticket through the SINAC website. I recommend taking a tour with a local guide. We took canoe tours with Don Feliciano! Great experience! (If you go for the day, you obviously won't see turtles since to see them you have to stay at least one night in Tortuguero because those tours are in the early morning.) Anyway, going for the day and taking a canoe tour on the rivers is spectacular! Greetings from Chile 🇨🇱 and thank you, Don Feliciano!

text:
An Unforgettable Day at La Paz Waterfall Gardens!

If you're looking for one of the most complete nature experiences in Costa Rica, La Paz Waterfall Gardens is an absolute must-visit! It easily earned a spot as one of the highlights of our trip.

The Waterfalls & Views
The paved trails lead you through the cloud forest right alongside a series of five breathtaking, roaring waterfalls. The viewing platforms get you amazingly close to the water—you can literally feel the cool mist on your face as you take in the views! Tip: There are quite a few stairs on the descent down the waterfall trail, but the best part is that a shuttle picks you up at the bottom to bring you back to the main building, saving your legs the climb up!

The Incredible Wildlife
The animal sanctuary inside the park is phenomenal. Every animal here is rescued and cared for, which makes the experience feel very special. We loved:

The walk-through aviary, where toucans fly right above your head.

The hummingbird garden, where dozens of colorful hummingbirds buzz right up to you.

Seeing jaguars, pumas, sloths, and monkeys up close in beautiful, spacious habitats.

The massive butterfly observatory filled with iridescent Blue Morphos.

The Delicious Buffet
Don't skip the buffet lunch! It was easily one of the best meals we had during our day trips. The spread includes traditional Costa Rican dishes (like classic casado staples), fresh meats, a full salad bar, fruits, pizza, and unlimited fresh tropical juices and coffee. Eating a warm, hearty meal overlooking the cloud forest was the perfect break.

A top-tier experience that combines Costa Rica’s natural beauty, rich wildlife, and incredible food all in one location! Highly, highly recommended! 🌿🦜🌊
title: La Paz Waterfall Gardens Nature Park
