text: Excelente lugar para familias. Tiene un centro de rescate donde puedes ver animales en cuativerio, inlcuyendo felinos silvestres, monos, aves, serpientes y ranas. La comida es bastante buena y variada y la atencion es excelente. El acceso a las cataratas es extraordinario y muy bien construido, pero puede ser un poco pesado para personas que caminan poco o tienen algun inpedimento fisico ya que hay que subir y bajar bastantes escaleras. Ojo, los fines de semena se llena mucho, especialmente durante las vacaciones.
textTranslated: Excellent place for families. It has a rescue center where you can see animals in captivity, including wild cats, monkeys, birds, snakes, and frogs. The food is quite good and varied, and the service is excellent. The access to the waterfalls is extraordinary and very well constructed, but it can be a bit strenuous for people who don't walk much or have some physical limitations, as there are quite a few stairs to climb. Be aware that it gets very crowded on weekends, especially during holidays.

text: El hotel está muy bonito lo mismo de los alrededores, los senderos están en perfectas condiciones,  sin embargo las jaulas donde están los  "supuestos animales rescatados " son muy pequeñas además de,  según mi umilde opinión no apropiadas para los animales, me parece que podrían tener áreas al aire libre para que ellos puedan disfrutar el sol y el agua de lluvia que es tan importante. A esas jaulas no les han hecho ninguna modificación en años según una persona que me acompañó, no estoy 100% convencida que todos los animales allí,  estaban en algún tipo de peligro, porque los pájaros como los Tucanes y algunos otros podrían estar libres y tener comida disponible en el lugar,  me parece que la mayoría los tiene en cautiverio para atraer turismo.
textTranslated: The hotel is very beautiful, as is the surrounding area. The trails are in perfect condition. However, the cages where the "supposedly rescued animals" are kept are very small and, in my humble opinion, not suitable for the animals. I think they could have outdoor areas so the animals can enjoy the sun and rainwater, which is so important. According to someone who was with me, those cages haven't been modified in years. I'm not 100% convinced that all the animals there were in any kind of danger, because birds like the toucans and some others could be free and have food available. It seems to me that most of them are kept in captivity to attract tourists.

Le sentier qu'on nous a proposé est constitué à moitié d'une forêt désertique et à moitié d'une forêt humide. Le sentier peut être fait en 2h mais je recommande de compter 3h si vous aimez prendre des photos et observer la faune. Apportez 2 litres d'eau par personne. Vous y verrez des fuméroles, des mares de boues chaudes (bouillantes même) et un volcancito (petit volcan). Nous avons vu des singes araignées et un groupes de capucins (une quinzaine). Il est aussi possible d'y voir des singes hurleurs. Très belle expérience et sentiers magnifiquement aménagés.
textTranslated: The Pailas area is very beautiful. It's accessible via a small road north of Liberia. The trail we were shown is half desert forest and half rainforest. The trail can be done in 2 hours, but I recommend allowing 3 hours if you enjoy taking photos and observing wildlife. Bring 2 liters of water per person. You'll see fumaroles, hot (even boiling) mud pools, and a volcanic crater (a small volcano). We saw spider monkeys and a group of capuchin monkeys (about fifteen). Howler monkeys are also a possibility. A very beautiful experience and the trails are magnificently maintained.

text:
Tortuguero ist ein wahres Juwel in Costa Rica und ein absolutes Muss für alle, die die unberührte Natur und die Tierwelt des Landes erleben möchten. Dieses abgelegene Dorf, das nur über Wasser- oder Luftwege erreichbar ist, bietet eine einzigartige Atmosphäre, die den Stress des Alltags sofort vergessen lässt.

Die Hauptattraktion von Tortuguero sind die beeindruckenden Kanäle und Lagunen, die von üppigem Regenwald umgeben sind. Eine Bootstour durch diese Gewässer ist ein unvergessliches Erlebnis. Man hat die Möglichkeit, eine Vielzahl von Tieren zu beobachten, darunter Affen, Faultiere, Kaimane und eine Vielzahl von Vogelarten. Die Vielfalt der Flora und Fauna ist einfach atemberaubend und macht jeden Ausflug zu einem Abenteuer.

Das Dorf selbst hat einen charmanten, authentischen Charakter. Die freundlichen Einheimischen heißen Besucher herzlich willkommen und bieten einen Einblick in ihre Kultur und Lebensweise. Es gibt kleine Restaurants, in denen man köstliche lokale Gerichte genießen kann, und Souvenirläden, die handgefertigte Produkte anbieten. Ein weiteres Highlight von Tortuguero ist die Schildkrötenbeobachtung. Je nach Jahreszeit kann man die beeindruckenden Meeresschildkröten beobachten, die an die Strände kommen, um ihre Eier abzulegen. Dies ist ein einmaliges Erlebnis, das die Bedeutung des Naturschutzes unterstreicht und einen tiefen Eindruck hinterlässt.

Das gesamte Erlebnis in Tortuguero ist geprägt von der Harmonie zwischen Mensch und Natur. Es ist der perfekte Ort, um sich zu entspannen, die Schönheit der Natur zu genießen und unvergessliche Erinnerungen zu sammeln. Ich kann Tortuguero nur wärmstens empfehlen - es ist ein Ort, der das Herz berührt und die Seele nährt!
textTranslated:
Tortuguero is a true gem in Costa Rica and an absolute must-see for anyone wanting to experience the country's pristine nature and wildlife. This remote village, accessible only by water or air, offers a unique atmosphere that instantly melts away the stresses of everyday life.

Tortuguero's main attraction is its impressive network of canals and lagoons surrounded by lush rainforest. A boat trip through these waterways is an unforgettable experience. You'll have the opportunity to observe a variety of animals, including monkeys, sloths, caimans, and numerous bird species. The diversity of flora and fauna is simply breathtaking and makes every excursion an adventure.

The village itself has a charming, authentic character. The friendly locals warmly welcome visitors and offer insights into their culture and way of life. There are small restaurants where you can enjoy delicious local dishes and souvenir shops selling handcrafted items. Another highlight of Tortuguero is turtle watching. Depending on the season, you can observe the impressive sea turtles that come ashore to lay their eggs. This is a unique experience that underscores the importance of nature conservation and leaves a lasting impression.

The entire experience in Tortuguero is characterized by the harmony between people and nature. It's the perfect place to relax, enjoy the beauty of nature, and create unforgettable memories. I highly recommend Tortuguero—it's a place that touches the heart and nourishes the soul!

text: Lieber zwei Mal überlegen! Wir sind nach Tortuguero gekommen, weil wir Tiere lieben und nur Gutes von den Schildkröten-Touren gehört haben. Leider wurden wir sehr enttäuscht. Wer Tiere wirklich liebt, sollte eine solche Tour nicht unterstützen. Das hat leider nichts mit dem hoch gelobten Tierschutz vor Ort zu tun. Es sind viel zu viele Menschen (mindestens 50-70 Personen) an einem Strandabschnitt, wenn dort Schildkröten gesichtet wurden. Diese Menschen machen einen solchen Lärm und die Guides scheint es nicht zu kümmern. Es ist sehr schlecht geregelt. Dadurch wurden mehrere Schildkröten daran gehindert, ihre Eier am Strand abzulegen. Die Schildkröten gingen wieder zurück ins Meer. Unser Guide hat sogar eine Meeresschildkröte angefasst, während sie Eier gelegt hat. Nun haben wir auch davon erfahren, dass durch die Lichter der Hotels viele schlüpfende Schildkröten fehlgeleitet werden und nicht den Weg ins Meer finden. Wir schämen uns sehr dafür, dass wir sowas aufgrund von Unwissenheit unterstützt haben. Wir raten daher allen Leuten, denen etwas am Wohl der Tiere liegt, von diesen Touren ab!
textTranslated: Think twice before booking! We came to Tortuguero because we love animals and had only heard good things about the turtle tours. Unfortunately, we were very disappointed. Anyone who truly loves animals should not support such a tour. It has nothing to do with the much-praised animal welfare practices in the area. There are far too many people (at least 50-70) on a stretch of beach whenever turtles are spotted. These people make an incredible amount of noise, and the guides don't seem to care. The situation is very poorly managed. As a result, several turtles were prevented from laying their eggs on the beach. The turtles had to return to the sea. Our guide even touched a sea turtle while it was laying eggs. We have now also learned that the lights from the hotels disorient many hatchlings, preventing them from finding their way to the ocean. We are deeply ashamed that we supported this out of ignorance. We therefore advise everyone who cares about animal welfare to stay away from these tours!

text:
If you’re planning a trip to Costa Rica, La Paz Waterfall Gardens needs to be on your radar. Located just about 45 minutes from the San José airport in the lush central highlands, this place feels like stepping straight into a tropical dream.​It is a stunning private nature reserve that combines heavy-hitting scenery with one of the most incredible up-close wildlife experiences in the country. But before you lace up your boots, there is one major thing you need to be prepared for.While the main pathways around the wildlife exhibits are beautifully paved and easy to stroll, the actual Waterfall Trail is a completely different beast.
​The Workout: The trail takes you down a steep mountain gorge to view five massive, roaring waterfalls. To get those jaw-dropping views, you will be navigating hundreds of steep, damp, and slick concrete stairs. Going down is a serious test for your knees, and if you choose to explore every lower platform, climbing back up into the humid cloud forest altitude will absolutely wind you. Worth it!!! Recommend hiking boots and water with electrolytes.
title: La Paz Waterfall Gardens Nature Park

Espero poder volver a encontrarnos pronto!
textTranslated: I just got back from my adventure in Costa Rica. Muy recomendable.

We visited Cahuita National Park and found it to be a beautiful place. We entered through Puerto Vargas, where parking is free and you only pay the park entrance fee, which is a nice bonus.

In addition, there is the option of snorkeling (only with a guide), which adds an interesting extra element to the experience. The park is very well maintained, and the staff is generally friendly, making the visit even more enjoyable.

Highly recommended.

Los 2.5 km de sendero sobre manglar y "selva" son muy lindos al lado de grandes árboles y animales como perezosos, mapaches, pizotes, monos, mariposas, etc. Caminar más allá de punta Vargas podría no ser tan neceserio sobre todo si estás cerca del mediodía. Las instalaciones están en un estado adecuado y los guías son muy amables. De verdad que se esmeran por hacerte sentir bien y muy seguro.

The 2.5 km trail through mangroves and jungle is beautiful, winding alongside towering trees and animals like sloths, raccoons, coatis, monkeys, butterflies, and more. Walking beyond Punta Vargas might not be necessary, especially around midday. The facilities are well-maintained, and the guides are very friendly. text:

Am Eingang wird der Rucksack kontrolliert und sämtliche Plastiktüte (für Trinken oder Sonnencreme usw.) eingezogen. Weiterhin führt nur ein Weg durch das Innere des Parks, der an den Stränden endet. Die Strände sahen nach relativ starkem Regen in den Tagen zuvor bei weitem nicht karibisch aus und sind auch vergleichsweise schmal.
Gesehen haben wir Affen, Waschbären, Schlangen, Vögel und Schmetterlinge. Dies sieht man aber auch außerhalb des Parks, wenn man die Hauptstraße verlässt.
textTranslated:
The national park is beautiful, but nothing special. First of all, there's an entrance fee, and snorkeling is only allowed with a guide for $45. Very disappointing. At the entrance, backpacks are checked, and all plastic bags (for drinks, sunscreen, etc.) are confiscated. Furthermore, there's only one path through the park, which ends at the beaches. After relatively heavy rain in the days prior, the beaches didn't look remotely Caribbean and are also comparatively narrow.

We saw monkeys, raccoons, snakes, birds, and butterflies. However, you can see these things outside the park as well if you leave the main road.

text: Sin duda la peor experiencia tanto culinaria como de trato recibido de todo Costa Rica. Llegamos y tardaron en atendernos para sentarnos cuando solo había dos mesas ocupadas en todo el local. Nos sentarnos y pedimos para dos personas dos platos y dos bebidas (13:30), un poco mas tarde unos diez minutos después entró una familia costarricense y tras hacer el pedido les sirvieron las bebidas al instante. 45 minutos después nos sirvieron a nosotros la bebida que además eran mucho mas pequeñas que las que servían en el local. Al de una hora nos sirvieron los dos platos: uno de pollo (malo no estaba) y otro de filete de pescado (para haberlo dejado en el plato, estaba seco y era enana la porción). El trato que recibieron los siguientes clientes extranjeros fue igual de malo que a nosotros. Si eres turista NO TE LO ACONSEJO POR NADA EN EL MUNDO.
textTranslated: Without a doubt, the worst culinary and service experience I've ever had in Costa Rica. We arrived and were incredibly slow to be seated, even though there were only two tables occupied in the entire restaurant. We finally sat down and ordered two dishes and two drinks for two people (1:30 PM). About ten minutes later, a Costa Rican family came in and their drinks were served immediately after they placed their order. It took us 45 minutes to get our drinks, which were much smaller than the ones they usually serve. An hour later, our two dishes arrived: one chicken (which wasn't bad) and one fish fillet (which was so dry and the portion was tiny it could have been left on the plate). The service the next foreign customers received was just as bad as ours. If you're a tourist, I DO NOT RECOMMEND THIS PLACE FOR ANYTHING IN THE WORLD.

text:
We decided to stop here after seeing many posts and reviews about this place. It’s more of a “zoo” style nature park where you can see toucans, sloths, butterfly’s, frogs, large cats-cougars, leopards etc up close. We also were able to walk the grounds and see the many waterfalls along the canyon.

The facility is clean, the animals seemed well cared for. Just know it is a zoo and they are not in their natural environment. The aviary was soooo cool, it’s a huge open space with tons of different birds free flying around. And the toucans were unreal seeing them so up close. There were thousands of butterfly as around in the butterfly garden, they land on you. Overall very cool immersive experience.

The waterfall walk was great. You are immersed in jungle and follow paved paths along the canyon edge with stairs leading to and from each waterfall

There is a free shuttle at the bottom to transport you back to the free parking lot. We much appreciated this as the stairs get tiring.

Overall worth the money, but it is an expensive experience. We paid 126 USD for 2 adults. We did not eat here. Just make sure you are educated on what you are visiting before you go., I personally did not appreciate the caged cats, however the bird and butterfly area were huge and awesome to see.

text:
I'd rate this stay 3.5 overall.

This is a remote hotel that is ~2hr drive from Liberia airport. If you are looking for a place to disconnect for a few days, it could work well for you. With strong and consistent wifi, you could also work remotely as a desk was provided in my room.

I booked this looking to extend my trip to a wellness resort nearby for a few days, otherwise I am not sure I can say the 2hr drive here is worth it with the last 45min - 1hr very bumpy and windy. If you get motion sickness, beware.

While my room was very nice, with a very comfortable bed and very nice deck with hammock overlooking the ocean (very grateful for the upgrade), the bathroom was small, the shower spurted water everywhere. The rest of the experience was too inconsistent for me to rate higher.

The prices here are high as others have mentioned, something that is becoming typical in Costa Rica with unmatched service and products.

160 for a 90 minute massage. While the massage was good, there were workers drilling and talking during my massage which was a bummer. Everytime I was about to say something they stopped and it wasn't overtly loud but annoying enough to ruin what would otherwise have been an amazing experience.

I was pleasantly surprised by the quality of my first dinner (Peruvian ceviche an skirt steak). Though the sides were tiny and if I was with my BF he'd have to order about 6 of them to suffice his carb intake, the quality of the ceviche and steak were very good. They provided good bread which made up for tiny sides. The breakfast the next day was also good with great service provided by Becher at both meals. Breakfast includes coffee, juice and an entree plus fruit. I cannot eat melon and pineapple and Becher brought me a big plate of mango and papaya.

Unfortunately that was the highlight of my trip, after that every meal was worse with the last day being the worst leaving a bad taste for me to likely not return.

There is a gym, and dining faciliites which are closed from 11-12 and 5-6pm. Leaving at 12PM, I asked for a smoothie to be made with my protein powder and a parfait to take with me, or eat on grounds just before the restuarant open. I was appreciative that they accomodated, but not happy when I received my smoothie which did not have the powder mixed in and was 1/3 of the size of the one I ordered the day before for $14. The parfait for $10 had 1 blueberry and 1 strawberry....

The gym is decent, though there is no AC until you turn it on yourself. The pool area is small but OK, and as busy as it was I often found myself alone.

The inconsistent service and food quality is probably the biggest negative. With minor tweaks, this hotel could be a much better experience.

Another tip, I wouldn't recommend the car service they book on your behalf. I used BlackCar for my inbound transfer and found the ride much smoother.

text: Muy recomendable. Entramos por la entrada de Playa Blanca y recomiendo hacer esto ya que así haces casi todo el sendero, después llegas en la playa para descansar bañarte y comer y al terminar acabas la ruta por un sendero de 2 kms por el medio de la selva en una plataforma de madera. En la zona de Cahuita intentan que metas tu coche en un parking de pago pero se puede aparcar en cualquier hueco en el pueblo gratuitamente. La entrada es la donación que quieras dar, nosotros dimos 5$ por persona. Pudimos entrar con comida pero cualquier cosa con plástico te hacían tirarlo (por ejemplo frutos secos en una bolsa de plástica, meterlos en un tupper). Los baños de esta entrada están asquerosos. El parque es muy bonito, vimos distintos tipos de monos, coaties, ardillas, muchos pájaros… La playa donde comimos era muy bonita y salvaje. En total estuvimos unos 6 horas en el parque, pero en movimiento entre 2-3 ya que fuimos parando mucho a ver animales. En la salida de Puerto Vargas pasa un bus cada hora hacia Cahuita o en nuestro caso había taxis piratas que te acercaban. A nosotros nos acercaron a 4 personas por 5.000 colones. Parque muy chulo!!
textTranslated: Highly recommended. We entered through the Playa Blanca entrance, and I recommend doing this because it covers almost the entire trail. Afterward, you reach the beach to relax, swim, and eat, and then finish the hike with a 2 km trail through the jungle on a wooden platform. In the Cahuita area, they try to get you to park in a paid lot, but you can park anywhere in town for free. The entrance fee is a donation; we gave $5 per person. We were allowed to bring food in, but anything in plastic was thrown away (for example, nuts in a plastic bag; put them in a Tupperware container). The restrooms at this entrance are disgusting. The park is beautiful; we saw different types of monkeys, coatis, squirrels, and many birds. The beach where we ate was beautiful and wild. In total, we spent about 6 hours in the park, but we were only moving around for 2-3 hours because we stopped a lot to see animals. At the Puerto Vargas exit, a bus leaves for Cahuita every hour, or in our case, there were unlicensed taxis that would take you closer. They took four of us for 5,000 colones. Very cool park!!

text: I was so excited leading up to this adventure but disappointed after leaving. I paid about $60 for a self guided tram ride. I was in a tram all by myself but upon ascent i couldn't help notice how low and open the rails are. If I panicked or wanted to return there was no way to communicate with park employees. There was a walkie in the car but no one instructed me on when/why/how to use. There should at minimum be a mesh screen around the trams and at the top on the observation platform because if you slip you are gone. Guests sign waivers prior to entering the park which appears to release the park from the burden of any incidents. Perhaps safety is focused more on the zip liners rather than tram riders but both the guard rails and barriers on the tram and at the lookout points are way too low and open. Considering the elevation level the guard rails should at least be 48" but even on me they aren't even waist high...and I'm 62" tall. As far as animals, I think the girest is too dense to see anything. I saw one small iguana sunning up at the overlook platform.

textTranslated: Cahuita National Park is practically a must-see. The full hike is long, and on a hot day it might be a bit tiring, but it's worth it. We entered through Puerto Vargas, where the entrance fee is 3,000 colones or US$6. If you choose to do part of the tour with a guide, it's US$25 per person (March 2026). If you have the money, I highly recommend going with a guide; they have a lot of knowledge, and it's easier to spot animals that are farther away. If you enjoy hearing interesting facts or being able to ask specific questions, it will also be an even better experience with a guide. We saw sloths, howler monkeys, white-faced capuchin monkeys (be careful with these!), coatis, raccoons, a toucan, a well-camouflaged caiman, a yellow-crowned mottled snake, a hawk, and from the shore, the fins of a reef shark. Perhaps there were other animals that I can't recall right now. After finishing at the main entrance, we took a tuk-tuk to Puerto Vargas where we had left the car in the parking lot, and it cost us ¢4000

Chère Manon,
Merci d’avoir pris le temps de partager votre expérience.
Nous sommes heureux que vous ayez apprécié la vue depuis le sommet, mais nous sommes sincèrement désolés d’apprendre que votre visite ne correspondait pas à vos attentes.
Concernant la balançoire mentionnée, nous vous remercions de nous l’avoir signalé. Si une ancienne image est toujours visible et prête à confusion, nous allons revoir cela afin de nous assurer que notre communication reflète fidèlement les attractions actuellement offertes. Nous comprenons tout à fait qu’une attente créée par une photo puisse influencer votre décision.
Le tram aérien est principalement conçu comme une expérience paisible d’observation de la canopée et de la nature. Pour les visiteurs recherchant davantage d’adrénaline, la tyrolienne est effectivement une excellente option complémentaire.
Nous apprécions sincèrement votre retour, qui nous aide à améliorer la clarté de nos informations et l’expérience globale de nos visiteurs. Nous espérons avoir l’occasion de vous accueillir de nouveau lors d’une prochaine visite au Costa Rica.
Cordialement,
L’équipe Rainforest Adventures Jacó

text: Un promontorio ricoperto di giungla che digrada verso l'oceano. Qui le scimmie cappuccine la fanno da padrone, attenzione ai vostri viveri sono specializzate in furti con scippo, e procioni passeggiano tranquilli. Ovviamente non mancano i bradipi e altre specie animali. Purtroppo il livello dell'oceano si sta alzando e la barriera corallina si sta sgretolando. Ecco quindi che l'erosione della costa avanza inesorabilmente. Le spiagge scompaiono e le palme cadono come birilli. Comunque un parco nazionale tra i più belli del Costa Rica.
textTranslated: A jungle-covered promontory that slopes down to the ocean. Capuchin monkeys reign supreme here—watch out for your supplies, they specialize in pickpocketing—and raccoons roam freely. Of course, sloths and other wildlife are also present. Unfortunately, the ocean level is rising, and the coral reef is crumbling. Coastal erosion is thus advancing inexorably. Beaches are disappearing, and palm trees are falling like bowling pins. Nevertheless, it's one of Costa Rica's most beautiful national parks.

text:
Le Parc National Cahuita est un endroit absolument magnifique et l’une des plus belles expériences nature que nous ayons eues au Costa Rica. Ce parc est unique car il combine forêt tropicale, plages paradisiaques et faune exceptionnelle dans un environnement encore très préservé.
La balade le long du sentier côtier est tout simplement magique. On marche entre la jungle et la mer des Caraïbes, avec des paysages incroyables à chaque instant. Les plages sont superbes, l’eau turquoise et la végétation luxuriante créent une atmosphère paisible et dépaysante.
Ce qui rend Cahuita vraiment spécial, c’est la faune incroyablement facile à observer. Nous avons vu plusieurs paresseux, des singes capucins et hurleurs, des ratons laveurs, des iguanes et de nombreux oiseaux tropicaux. La nature est partout et les animaux semblent vivre ici en totale liberté.
Le sentier est facile et très agréable à parcourir, ce qui permet de profiter pleinement de l’environnement et de prendre son temps pour observer les animaux ou simplement admirer les paysages. À certains endroits, on peut même se baigner dans une mer chaude et claire, entouré par la nature.
L’ambiance est également très agréable et authentique, avec un esprit caribéen détendu qui rend la visite encore plus plaisante. On sent que le parc est respecté et que la nature y est vraiment protégée.
Si vous visitez la côte caraïbe du Costa Rica, le Parc National Cahuita est un incontournable absolu. Un endroit magnifique, sauvage et paisible, où l’on peut vivre une véritable immersion dans la nature. Une expérience inoubliable.
textTranslated:
Cahuita National Park is an absolutely magnificent place and one of the most beautiful nature experiences we had in Costa Rica. This park is unique because it combines rainforest, idyllic beaches, and exceptional wildlife in a still very pristine environment.
The walk along the coastal trail is simply magical. You walk between the jungle and the Caribbean Sea, with incredible scenery at every turn. The beaches are superb, the turquoise water and lush vegetation create a peaceful and exotic atmosphere.
What makes Cahuita truly special is the incredibly easy-to-observe wildlife. We saw several sloths, capuchin and howler monkeys, raccoons, iguanas, and numerous tropical birds. Nature is everywhere, and the animals seem to live here in complete freedom.
The trail is easy and very pleasant to walk, allowing you to fully enjoy the environment and take your time to observe the animals or simply admire the scenery. In some places, you can even swim in the warm, clear sea, surrounded by nature. The atmosphere is also very pleasant and authentic, with a relaxed Caribbean vibe that makes the visit even more enjoyable. You can feel that the park is respected and that nature is truly protected.

If you're visiting the Caribbean coast of Costa Rica, Cahuita National Park is an absolute must-see. A magnificent, wild, and peaceful place where you can experience a true immersion in nature. An unforgettable experience.

text:
Si estás visitando el Caribe Sur de Costa Rica, el Parque Nacional Cahuita no es opcional, es obligatorio. Es, sin duda, uno de los parques más hermosos y accesibles del país, con la ventaja única de que puedes caminar por senderos planos a la sombra de la jungla mientras tienes el mar color turquesa a solo pasos de distancia.El parque tiene dos entradas principales. La entrada de Playa Blanca (en el pueblo de Cahuita) funciona bajo la modalidad de "contribución voluntaria" (donación), lo cual es genial para apoyar a la comunidad local. La entrada de Puerto Vargas es la oficial del SINAC y tiene un costo fijo (aprox. $5 para nacionales y $10-12 para extranjeros). Yo recomiendo entrar por el pueblo, caminar todo el sendero y salir por Puerto Vargas si tienes transporte esperándote, o viceversa.El sendero principal tiene unos 8 km de longitud (solo ida). Lo mejor es que es totalmente plano, lo que lo hace apto para casi cualquier condición física. ¡La biodiversidad es increíble! Sin mucho esfuerzo pudimos ver:
Monos Capuchinos (Cara Blanca) y Monos Congos (se escuchan desde lejos).
Perezosos de dos y tres dedos (miren hacia arriba en los almendros).
Mapaches y Pizotes (cuidado con su comida, son expertos ladrones).
Víboras de pestañas (la famosa Oropel), iguanas y garzas.Las playas son de arena blanca y aguas cristalinas. Punta Cahuita es el mejor lugar para fotos, donde el arrecife de coral es espectacular.Para hacer snorkel en el arrecife, es obligatorio contratar un guía certificado y una lancha; no está permitido entrar por cuenta propia desde la orilla para proteger el coral.
Llega temprano: El parque abre a las 8:00 AM. A esa hora hay menos gente y los animales están más activos.
Hidratación: Lleva mucha agua. El calor y la humedad del Caribe no perdonan.
Aunque podrías ir en sandalias a la playa, para el sendero recomiendo calzado cerrado o sandalias deportivas (tipo Teva/Keen) porque hay zonas que pueden tener barro.
Respeto a la fauna: Por favor, NO alimentes a los animales. Los monos pueden ponerse agresivos si ven comida y les hace mucho daño a su dieta natural.
El bloqueador solar Preferiblemente biodegradables para no afectar el ecosistema marino.
Cahuita ofrece una experiencia mucho más íntima y menos saturada que Manuel Antonio. Es un lugar mágico donde realmente sientes la esencia del "Pura Vida". Ideal para ir en familia, en pareja o incluso solo para meditar frente al mar.No olvides tu cámara, la vas a necesitar
textTranslated:
If you're visiting the Southern Caribbean of Costa Rica, Cahuita National Park isn't optional, it's a must-see. It's undoubtedly one of the most beautiful and accessible parks in the country, with the unique advantage of being able to hike along flat trails shaded by the jungle while the turquoise sea is just steps away. The park has two main entrances. The Playa Blanca entrance (in the town of Cahuita) operates on a "voluntary contribution" (donation) basis, which is great for supporting the local community. The Puerto Vargas entrance is the official SINAC entrance and has a fixed cost (approximately $5 for Costa Rican citizens and $10-12 for foreigners). I recommend entering through the town, hiking the entire trail, and exiting through Puerto Vargas if you have transportation waiting for you, or vice versa. The main trail is about 8 km long (one way). The best part is that it's completely flat, making it suitable for almost any fitness level. The biodiversity is incredible! Without much effort, we were able to see:
Capuchin monkeys (white-faced capuchins) and howler monkeys (you can hear them from afar).
Two-toed and three-toed sloths (look up in the almond trees).
Raccoons and coatis (be careful with your food, they are expert thieves).
Eyelash vipers (the famous "oropel"), iguanas, and herons. The beaches have white sand and crystal-clear waters. Punta Cahuita is the best place for photos, where the coral reef is spectacular. To snorkel on the reef, it is mandatory to hire a certified guide and a boat; entering on your own from the shore is not allowed to protect the coral.
Arrive early: The park opens at 8:00 AM. At that time, there are fewer people and the animals are more active.
Hydration: Bring plenty of water. The Caribbean heat and humidity are relentless.
Although you could wear sandals to the beach, for the trail I recommend closed shoes or athletic sandals (like Teva/Keen) because some areas can be muddy. Respect the wildlife: Please DO NOT feed the animals. Monkeys can become aggressive if they see food, and it greatly harms their natural diet.
Sunscreen: Preferably biodegradable to avoid harming the marine ecosystem. Cahuita offers a much more intimate and less crowded experience than Manuel Antonio. It's a magical place where you truly feel the essence of "Pura Vida." Ideal for families, couples, or even just for meditating by the sea. Don't forget your camera; you'll need it.

The Rio Suarez has been closed a while due to rain so we knew that we would not be able to hike over to the Vargas side but being a dry day and being informed at our hotel that the parc would be closed a couple of days for necessary cleaning and upkeep we decided to go anyway.

There is s suggested $5 pp donation on entry which we gladly paid.
Even before entering (on the Playa Blanca side) there was a small group pointing at a tree just before the entry gates, and there was a Sloth hanging from a pretty low branch!
The path runs north just in from the Playa Blanca. There were some small groups with guides but it wasn’t crowded despite the imminent closure.
The walk to Rio Suarez is only about 1.5 but we saw two Lashed Pit Vipers (spotted by others but close enough to photograph on my phone), another sloth, a squirrel monkey and a group of Coatis! Again all close enough to without telescopes!
At the Rio Suarez we turned and walked back along the beautiful beach seeing brown Pelicans and Snowy Egrets in flight… and another Sloth in a tree🦥😃
After exiting we took another look at the first Sloth and strolled over to another group of tourists with cameras to see a large Iguana in a tree!
Having visited Parc Manuel Antonio the previous week and only getting far off views of beige high up in a couple of trees that we were told were Sloths, I am definitely Camp Cahuita!!

text:
De kamers zijn echt heerlijk! Ondanks dat 1 kant van ons hed wat afliep, was het bed echt heerlijk. Je hebt een binnen en buiten douche. Zou aan de buitendouche niet snel de kop iets bijstellen, aangezien die bij ons toen brak. Ze kwamen het wel erg snel maken. Je hebt een keukentje met het hoognodige aan servies wat prima is. Anders komen ze het brengen, zoals een waterkoker. De hangmat is echt mega chill!

Als je je kleren wilt laten wassen is dat mega prijzig. 5,- dollar per shirt bijv en 2,- dollar voor een paar sokken of 1 stuk ondergoed.

Ondanks dat ik het wel vervelend vind als je de ‘do not disturb’ kaart hebt hangen en ze alsnog gaan schoonmaken (overigens wel een vriendelijk vrouwtje), is de service is echt top! Door iedereen zijn we mega vriendelijk geholpen. Bij de receptie, in het restaurant… 1x vonden we de pasta wat droog en toen kregen we een taartje ter compensatie. echt top! Ook de tuinmannen en schilders zijn erg vriendelijk.

De locatie vonden we alleen niks. We voelden ons beiden echt wat opgesloten daardoor in het hotel (ondanks dat het prachtig is). De weg er naar toe (route 160, vanuit het noorden - de zuidkant weten we niet) is echt vol gaten en niet goed onderhouden. Een stukje van 20 km max doe je een uur over. Een 4x4 auto is sowieso echt aan te raden en dan het liefst een stevigere auto dan die wij hadden. Vanuit het hotel wordt er wel overigens het 1 en ander georganiseerd als je zou willen (surfen, paardrijden, etc), maar snel naar een ander leuk stadje gaan zit er niet echt in. Hoogtepunt vonden we Playa Frijolar. Dat strand is nog best goed aan te rijden en je hebt daar Tiki hut (een chille beachtent). Dit is op 10 min rijden en hadden we eerder moeten weten.

(De laatste 2 foto’s zijn van playa frijolar en het filmpje is van de tiki hut, ondanks dat het enorm regende hebben we ons daar enorm goed vermaakt)
textTranslated:
The rooms are really lovely! Even though one side of our bed sloped a bit, the bed was really comfortable. You have an indoor and an outdoor shower. I wouldn't be quick to adjust the shower head on the outdoor shower, as ours broke when we did. They did come and fix it very quickly, though. There is a kitchenette with the bare minimum of crockery, which is fine. Otherwise, they bring things to you, like a kettle. The hammock is really super chill!

If you want to have your clothes washed, it is mega pricey. $5 per shirt, for example, and $2 for a pair of socks or one piece of underwear.

Although I do find it annoying when you have the ‘do not disturb’ sign hanging and they still start cleaning (a friendly lady, by the way), the service is really top-notch! Everyone helped us in a super friendly way. At the reception, in the restaurant… once we found the pasta a bit dry and we got a small cake as compensation. Really great! The gardeners and painters are also very friendly.

We just didn't like the location. We both felt a bit trapped in the hotel because of that (even though it is beautiful). The road leading there (Route 160, from the north – we don't know about the south side) is full of potholes and poorly maintained. It takes an hour to cover a stretch of 20 km max. A 4x4 is highly recommended anyway, and preferably a sturdier vehicle than the one we had. The hotel does organize a few things if you'd like (surfing, horseback riding, etc.), but getting to another nice town quickly isn't really an option. We found Playa Frijolar to be the highlight. That beach is actually quite easy to reach by car, and there is Tiki Hut there (a chill beach bar). It is a 10-minute drive away, and we should have known about it sooner.

(The last 2 photos are of Playa Frijolar and the video is of the Tiki Hut; despite the heavy rain, we had a great time there.)

They have an amazing gondola ride for for anyone and everyone. The views of the jungle are amazing, lots of birds trees butterflies and more. There is even a butterfly exhibit with some of the most beautiful creatures you will have a hard time seeing up close at Manuel Forest.

But as far as the zip line goes. The team here know how to have fun, be safe and make sure the whole crew had a great time. Carolina and the team took such amazing care and made sure we had a blast. Even my youngest who is seven was able to ride every line and when needed they paired her up with a staff member to make sure she got across and didn't get stuck (due to being not being heavy enough) the team even educated us on the local plant and wildlife. Can't say enough about how awesome they were.

Like I said there are plenty of zip lines in Jaco. But none that will have you writing a positive review late at night. Kudos to the team and thank you for making my families trip the best.

responseFromOwnerText: Gracias por compartir su experiencia y tomarse el tiempo de dejar sus comentarios. street: Jaco, 5mins del centro; 3.5KMS al este del Maxi Pali 5 mins. from Jaco downtown; 3.5kms east of Maxi Pali
text:
Hicimos reservas online para las 10:00 a.m., y a los minutos nos contactaron para decir que  sólo estaba disponible a las 14:00 hrs. En el paseo en teleférico practicamente no se ve ningún animal, sólo un par de pájaros. El paseo es lindo para el que nunca lo ha hecho antes, pero pobre para el que ya los ha hecho en otros lugares. La llamda cascada era sólo una caida con muy poca agua. Al llegar arriba no nos avisaron para bajarnos y disfrutar la vista que nos habían ofrecido.
Caro para lo que ofrecen.
textTranslated:
We made online reservations for 10:00 a.m., and within minutes they contacted us to say it was only available at 2:00 p.m. On the cable car ride, you practically don't see any animals, just a couple of birds. The ride is nice for someone who's never done it before, but disappointing for those who have done it elsewhere. The so-called waterfall was just a trickle with very little water. When we got to the top, they didn't tell us to get off and enjoy the view they had promised.
Expensive for what they offer.

Animals… we only saw monkeys in the distance.

Excelentes espacios para descansar al aire libre. Meditar , escuchar el mar, aves en su mayoría pericos y otros de la misma familia.
Muchos árboles de manga, hermosos y deliciosas.
Muchísimas palmeras, que logran dar el más hermoso paisaje de la playa.
Hay otras playas cercanas, muy bonitas y con poca gente, que nos permite disfrutar más la hermosa vista del atardecer del océano Pacífico.
El hotel está hermoso, cada habitación esta equipada para disfrutar de una sala, zona de cocina con todo lo necesario para servir vino, refrescos, algunas boquitas , hay platos, cafecito, refrigerador de buen tamaño para ser de habitación, no hay microondas ni cocina.
T.V, aire y ventiladores, un pequeño parlante, vaporizador, muy hermosa ducha sin techo, bonito detalle. También el baño completo.
Están las villas, con cocina, microondas y todo lo requerido.
Consejo, puede llevar cosas para picar, refrescos, cerveza, vino , latas, sino hay un supermercado donde encuentra la mayoría de comestibles y bebidas, en San Juanillo, es continuando luego de la entrada al hotel, cerca de diez minutos, pero si tiene espacio en el carro y hielera, organice y lleve su vino, quesos, algún embutidos de su elección, frutas, refrescos, algunas latas etc no necesita llevar, ni comprar vasos, platos... desechables. Hay de todo lo necesario, hasta servilletas y un desayunador con dos sillas.
En la zona de descanso puede disfrutar sus bebidas, también pueden atender sus necesidades desde restaurante y bar.
Mesa de Villar, tenis de mesa, juegos de mesa , gimnasio, está muy bien.
Lastima el inconveniente que tuvimos al llegar, tan cansado el viaje desde San José. Pero bueno, era tarde y pues a aceptar la precaria solución.
textTranslated:
Away from the noise.
A pleasant space overall.
A lovely pool.
Excellent spaces for relaxing outdoors. Meditating, listening to the sea, birds (mostly parakeets and other members of the same family).
Many mango trees, beautiful and delicious.
A great many palm trees, creating the most beautiful beach landscape.
There are other nearby beaches, very beautiful and less crowded, allowing us to better enjoy the stunning sunset views over the Pacific Ocean.
The hotel is beautiful; each room is equipped with a living area, a kitchenette with everything needed to serve wine, soft drinks, and snacks. There are plates, a small coffee maker, and a good-sized refrigerator for a room. There is no microwave or stove.
TV, air conditioning and fans, a small speaker, a steamer, and a very nice open-air shower—a nice touch. There is also a full bathroom.
There are also villas with a kitchen, microwave, and everything else required. Tip: You can bring snacks, soft drinks, beer, wine, and canned goods. If not, there's a supermarket in San Juanillo where you can find most groceries and drinks; it's about a ten-minute drive past the hotel entrance. But if you have space in your car and a cooler, pack your own wine, cheeses, cold cuts of your choice, fruit, soft drinks, and canned goods. You don't need to bring or buy disposable cups, plates, etc. They have everything you need, even napkins, and a breakfast area with two chairs.
You can enjoy your drinks in the lounge area, and they can also cater to your needs at the restaurant and bar. There's a pool table, ping pong, board games, and a gym—it's very nice. It's a shame about the problem we had upon arrival; the trip from San José was so tiring. But oh well, it was late, so we had to accept the makeshift solution.

text:
My group of 12 had a wonderful experience here! We paid for the full package and did just about everything. The high ropes course was a bit more intimidating than expected but I got through it. The rock wall is the last part of the high ropes and I didn’t enjoy THAT part at all, but I didn’t die so it’s fine.

The butterfly garden was really nice with lots of them flying all around. We also saw fruit bats who were sleeping soundly and clearly didn’t want to be disturbed (they were tucked under the leaves so nicely).

The tram was nice and slow with great views of everything below. It took about 15-20 minutes to get to the top and it was nice to rest a bit after the hike and high ropes.

The ziplines were awesome and the guides were great. They were very friendly, helpful, and funny! The views were great and made it all worth it (even to the members in our group who were initially scared to do this!). A time was had and it was the highlight of our trip.
title: Rainforest Adventures Jaco

text:
Después de haber visitado varios parques nacionales, incluido el de Manuel Antonio, tengo que decir que me quedo con el Parque Nacional Cahuita sin ninguna duda.

Lo que más me gustó es que se siente mucho más natural y menos saturado de gente. Los senderos junto al mar son espectaculares y la biodiversidad es increíble; pudimos ver muchísimos animales en un entorno mucho más tranquilo y auténtico. Las playas son paradisíacas y el hecho de que se pueda entrar por el pueblo de Cahuita mediante una contribución voluntaria le da un valor humano muy especial. ¡Una visita obligada en el Caribe!
textTranslated:
After visiting several national parks, including Manuel Antonio, I have to say that Cahuita National Park is my absolute favorite.

What I loved most is that it feels much more natural and less crowded. The trails along the coast are spectacular, and the biodiversity is incredible; we saw so many animals in a much more peaceful and authentic setting. The beaches are idyllic, and the fact that you can enter through the town of Cahuita with a voluntary donation adds a very special human touch. A must-see in the Caribbean!
title: Parque Nacional Cahuita

text:
Un écrin de nature qui mériterait une sérieuse rénovation
Le concept de l'hôtel est séduisant avec ses petits bungalows individuels orientés vers le volcan Arenal, agrémentés d'une terrasse et de fauteuils à bascule typiques. Les jardins sont splendides, très bien entretenus et regorgent d'oiseaux, ce qui offre un dépaysement immédiat.
Cependant, l'intérieur de la chambre est très vétuste : la décoration est datée et la salle de bain, manque cruellement de modernité et de fraîcheur. Côté confort, la literie est très moyenne, ce qui est regrettable pour un hôtel de cette catégorie.
L'expérience nocturne est également compliquée : aucune insonorisation. On entend les voisins comme s'ils partageaient notre chambre.
La piscine principale manque de charme et donne une impression de "tourisme de masse" assez impersonnelle et très bruyant. En revanche, les hot springs sont le point fort : plus intimistes, entourés de verdure.
textTranslated:
A natural haven in dire need of renovation.

The hotel's concept is appealing, with its small, individual bungalows facing the Arenal volcano, each with a terrace and traditional rocking chairs. The gardens are splendid, meticulously maintained, and teeming with birds, offering an immediate escape.

However, the room's interior is very outdated: the decor is dated, and the bathroom sorely lacks modernity and freshness. Comfort-wise, the bedding is mediocre, which is regrettable for a hotel of this category.
The nighttime experience is also problematic: there is no soundproofing. You can hear your neighbors as if they were sharing your room.
The main pool lacks charm and gives a rather impersonal and noisy "mass tourism" impression. On the other hand, the hot springs are the highlight: more intimate and surrounded by lush greenery.

text: Hermoso lugar con una playa divina, con olas o algunos lugares más tranqui para estar sentado disfrutando del agua la la vista. Muy amplio y extenso camino para caminar y disfrutar de la vegetación y la fauna, como ser monitos, mapaches, perezosos, aves hermosas, peces, cangrejos, lagartos, etc. No se puede entrar con comida y con ninguna bolsas de ningún tamaño salvo que sea con ziploc. Hay que tener cuidado con las cosas porque los mapaches y los monitos gustan de abrir las carteras y sacar cosas. Es con un bono contribución para mantener el parque. De 9 a 3 de la tarde. Se puede salir para comer afuera en algún restaurante o puesto y volver a entrar. Hay baños y duchas para enjuagarse el agua salada. Son duchas expuestas no para usar jabón. Después en su casa cada uno puede bañarse con tranquilidad. Aconsejo dejar el auto en la playa de estacionamiento que está al lado y guardar las bolsas plasticas para guardar después la ropa mojada y calzado.
textTranslated: Beautiful place with a gorgeous beach, with waves or some calmer spots to sit and enjoy the water and the view. A very wide and extensive path for walking and enjoying the vegetation and wildlife, such as monkeys, raccoons, sloths, beautiful birds, fish, crabs, lizards, etc. Food and bags of any size are not allowed inside unless they are resealable. Be careful with your belongings because the raccoons and monkeys like to open bags and take things. There is a suggested donation to help maintain the park. It's open from 9 am to 3 pm. You can leave to eat at one of the restaurants or food stalls and then return. There are restrooms and showers to rinse off the saltwater. These are open showers, not for using soap. You can shower at home afterward. I recommend leaving your car in the parking lot next door and keeping the plastic bags to store your wet clothes and shoes.

Hubo cortes de electricidad en las noches y durante el día, el AC obviamente no servía ni había Internet. Además los teléfonos de las habitaciones tampoco podían utilizarse.
Había una quema en la playa frente al hotel.
La calle para llegar hasta el hotel está bastante mala, pasan todos los carros pero es de lastre y se hace largo el camino.
Los precios del restaurante son bastante caros (una sopa azteca $17).
textTranslated:
The hotel is very nice, and the beach is easily accessible. I stayed in a very comfortable two-story villa, which was fully equipped.
The pool was in excellent condition, and the staff was friendly. I would have liked to hear music in the pool and bar area.
Recommended for a relaxing getaway.

The downsides: There were power outages at night and during the day, so the AC obviously didn't work, and there was no internet. The phones in the rooms were also unusable.
There was a fire on the beach in front of the hotel.
The road to the hotel is in pretty bad condition; all cars can drive through, but it's a gravel road, making the journey quite long.
The restaurant prices are quite expensive (an Aztec soup costs $17).

text:
My husband and I did the Zipline/aerial tram tour. We got very lucky that there was a lull at 2pm, so we got Israel and Carolina all to ourselves.

We were a little nervous that we would feel afraid on the ziplines, but we didn't experience anything but joy. 😊

It was 8 different ziplines down the mountain with various platforms. There is also a professional photographer who can come with you and take your photos, then the files are given to you either on a thumb drive or air dropped to you.

Israel and Carolina were both incredibly knowledgeable --about everything! They told us all about Costa Rica, the climate, the economy, the plants, the birds, the insects. We were so grateful to have them guide us, and each stopped to show us different things along the way that they knew might interest us. We also got lucky and saw two toucans on our way up on the aerial tram.

There is a small cafe, a nice restroom, and a gift shop as well. Definitely recommend this company and experience.

Par cette humidité, il aurait été bien d’avoir un modèle fonctionnel. Au vu du prix de la nuitée, c’est très dommage.

La literie était trop raide à notre goût, on s’est levé avec des maux de dos atroces.
Les thermes sont super sympa (vu sur le volcan géniale, pareil de la chambre), le complexe est bien entretenu.
Nous avons fait un dîner (très bon) et 2 petits déjeuners (1 sur les 2 a été plus que décevant et le dernier top).
Avis mitigé donc.
textTranslated:
Room 255 was spacious, but the air conditioning was ancient, sounded like a jet engine taking off, and the vent cover was broken. Given the humidity, a working unit would have been much appreciated. Considering the price of the room, this was a real shame.
The bathroom is dated and, more importantly, starting to show its age, especially the shower.
The bedding was too firm for our liking; we woke up with terrible back pain.
The thermal baths are lovely (the view of the volcano was fantastic, as was the view from the room), and the complex is well-maintained.
We had dinner (very good) and two breakfasts (one was extremely disappointing, and the other was excellent). Overall, a mixed review.

The hot springs were stagnant and gave me a terrible allergic reaction all over my body. My skin was incredibly red and covered in tiny spots. It was a terrible experience. They never told us the hot springs were broken because the pump wasn't working. The first pool, which was supposed to be the hottest, was lukewarm and filthy. The water was stagnant, forming a line of grime. Then, in the room, there was a strong, awful smell coming from the bathroom that never went away. We called to ask for a different room, and they only cleaned it, but the smell persisted. I think the septic tanks were overflowing because it smelled terrible.

On the positive side, the breakfast was very good and the staff very friendly, but the allergic reaction was horrendous. I had to pay a lot for treatment to stop the itching and reduce the swelling. Never again, thank you.

text: Este hotel consiste en varias cabañas, con terraza o balcón, con hamaca incluida. Cada unidad cuenta con refrigeradora, lavatrastos, escritorio, sofá, y, en nuestro caso, con dos duchas, una de ellas en el exterior para bañarse bajo un impecable cielo azul o la luz de las estrellas. La estadía es muy cómoda. La piscina es grande, con bar y restaurante. No recomiendo los cócteles, los cuales tienen mucho por mejorar (un martini no lleva cáscara de limón dulce). Aparte hay un restaurante para la cena, la calidad es desigual de un día a otro; no recomiendo ni la carne roja, ni los camarones al ajillo. El pescado estaba muy bien, así como las pastas con mariscos. El desayuno pudo ser mejor, por ejemplo, pan y frutas es algo que todo hotel de la zona ofrece. Es importante señalar que la carretera para llegar está en pésimas condiciones y que no hay restaurantes cerca. Si desea ir a San Juanillo y quedarse por la zona, definitivamente este hotel es un must.
textTranslated: This hotel consists of several cabins, each with a terrace or balcony and a hammock. Each unit has a refrigerator, sink, desk, sofa, and, in our case, two showers, one of them outdoors for bathing under a clear blue sky or the starlight. The stay is very comfortable. The pool is large, with a bar and restaurant. I don't recommend the cocktails, which have much room for improvement (a martini doesn't have sweet lemon peel). There's also a restaurant for dinner, but the quality is inconsistent from day to day; I don't recommend either the red meat or the garlic shrimp. The fish was very good, as were the seafood pasta dishes. Breakfast could have been better; for example, bread and fruit are standard fare at every hotel in the area. It's important to note that the road to get there is in terrible condition and there are no restaurants nearby. If you want to go to San Juanillo and stay in the area, this hotel is definitely a must-visit.

text: El lugar inmediatamente uno llega esta alejado de el ruido y produce una vibra para relajarse. Las cabinas o habitaciones son muy rústicas, lo hace a uno sentirse en casa. La que se alquilo con mi familia tenia cocina, comedor, terraza, 1 habitación grande en donde durmieron 3 personas y 1 sofá que se hacia cama. El mismo hotel tiene restaurante en esto uno puede pasar a realizar las 3 comidas. El desayuno del lugar es muy típico, pero casi no varía conforme pasa la semana, siento que eso pudiera cambiar. Me gusto que tenían opción de juegos de mesa que uno podía agarrar para jugar en familia. La playa es algo que me gusto mucho por que no estaba llena de personas, en el sentido que es bastante privada. Tienen unas como camas para que uno pueda relajarse, leer un rato o solamente ver la playa y oírla. Esta algo alejado de como donde hay tiendas. Recomienda llevar repelente de insectos por que durante el día y las noches pueden aparecer.
textTranslated: The place is immediately secluded and has a relaxing vibe. The cabins or rooms are very rustic, making you feel right at home. The one my family and I rented had a kitchen, dining area, terrace, a large bedroom that slept three, and a sofa bed. The hotel also has a restaurant where you can eat all three meals. The breakfast is very typical, but it doesn't change much throughout the week, which I think could be improved. I liked that they had board games available for families to play together. The beach was a big plus because it wasn't crowded; it felt quite private. They have sunbeds where you can relax, read, or just enjoy the view. It's a bit far from shops. I recommend bringing insect repellent because insects can appear both day and night.
title: Azul Ocean Club Hotel

name: tractorcito100
text: Playa de arena gris... de unos 2 kilómetros de largo, agradable y poco visitada. La carretera parcialmente de lastre. El hotel cuenta con buenas instalaciones y personal amable. Sin embargo, algunas cosas pueden mejorar, sería ideal la colocación de un basurero grante en la salida hacia la playa, en mi visita recogí materiales plásticos de la playa, hay pocos, pero, sí existen desechos traídos por el mar, sin embargo, debe haber un sitio donde depositarlos que sea de fácil acceso para las personas interesadas en colaborar con el ambiente, también deben mejorar los kajaks y los chalecos salvavidas, ya que se encuentran en pésimo estado de hecho su uso en las condiciones actuales es peligroso. El wet bar no está en servicio y el desayuno puede mejorar. Cerca del hotel hay playas muy hermosas. Las habitaciones son muy bonitas. Es interesante apuntar que una de las habitaciones para personas con necesidades especiales, concretamente la 9, tiene el inodoro del primer piso encerrado en un espacio muy estrecho entre la ducha y el lavatorio, eso podría significar un obstáculo para personas en condición especial. El espacio para la mesa de ping pong es amplio, no obstante en uno de los extremos hay un especio grande que da hacia un jardín y alguien podría caer por ahí, mientras se encuentra practicando el deporte. Eso se podría mejorar para evitar algún accidente.
textTranslated: Gray sand beach... about 2 kilometers long, pleasant and not very crowded. The road is partially gravel. The hotel has good facilities and friendly staff. However, some things could be improved. It would be ideal to place a large trash can at the exit to the beach. During my visit, I collected plastic materials from the beach; there weren't many, but there is some debris brought in by the sea. However, there should be an easily accessible place to dispose of it for people interested in helping the environment. The kayaks and life jackets also need improvement, as they are in terrible condition; in fact, using them in their current state is dangerous. The swim-up bar is not open, and the breakfast could be improved. There are very beautiful beaches near the hotel. The rooms are very nice. It's worth noting that one of the rooms for people with special needs, specifically room 9, has the first-floor toilet enclosed in a very narrow space between the shower and the sink. This could pose an obstacle for people with disabilities. The space for the ping pong table is ample; however, at one end there's a large opening that leads to a garden, and someone could fall through it while playing. This could be improved to prevent accidents.

En bref, l’endroit convient si l’on cherche un peu d’isolement et un séjour confortable, par contre il faut ressortir pour les repas (Marbella, San Juanillo, Ostional voire Nosara).
textTranslated: The resort is secluded (20 km of dirt track, not too difficult coming from the north, but the southern section is in poorer condition and requires a 4x4), far from the crowds, with its own private beach (there's a strong current, but swimming is still possible). Dinner is overpriced, lunch by the pool is only average value for money, and breakfast is served plated (only one plate available from six choices, no buffet, and the juice and coffee are very disappointing). The rooms are spacious and comfortable, and the various amenities like hammocks are a nice touch. In short, the place is suitable if you're looking for a bit of seclusion and a comfortable stay, but you'll need to go out for meals (Marbella, San Juanillo, Ostional, or even Nosara).

textTranslated: Typically, when flying to Costa Rica, you land at Juan Santamaría International Airport in the capital, San José. The airport is comfortable, neat, and compact. You can rent a car there and continue on to your pre-selected hotel. It's worth noting that the airport, like the capital itself, San José, is located in the center of the country. The nearest coastline is about 250 km away—a roughly five-hour drive, which can be quite daunting after a long flight. But as adventure lovers, that didn't stop us. Based on reviews on Booking.com, we chose a "good" hotel—Azul Ocean Club Hotel Santa Cruz—and drove from the airport to it. After five hours of driving on asphalt, we followed signs for the hotel and turned onto a gravel road. We then drove another 21 km through dusty terrain to the hotel from the highway. The air conditioning in the car also broke down….||||We went with one hope – to get to the Oasis for dinner!!! We arrived on March 29, 2019 at 8:30 pm local time. The hotel was unlit!!! There was no asphalt in front of the hotel. There were three cars parked in the same dust as ours!!!||||At the reception, they gave us a guide (security guard) – a local "muchach" – who had a machete about 80 centimeters long hanging on his back. It looks scary!!) We came to our room.||||The room had not been cleaned for a week!!! No water to wash up after the road!!!||||Hungry from the road, we asked at the reception where we could have dinner. We were told – there is no bar!! No restaurant!! No store!! Only breakfast in the morning!!! And this is a 5-star hotel!!!||||Everywhere – dust, dirt, desolation!!! No one at the hotel speaks English except at reception!!!||||We inspected the grounds in the morning: they are very small – 100 by 20 meters, with one swimming pool measuring 5 by 10 meters. The beach by the hotel is one big dump; it hasn't been cleaned for ten years!!! Trash, fallen palm trees, dirt.||||Dejected by this view, we went to breakfast hoping for exotic fruit and seafood. In the dining room, they brought us a five-item menu: one free (included in the room rate), the rest for a fee. Mostly bacon and eggs and omelets.||||Summary: No fruit. No seafood. No leisure. It looks like an abandoned pioneer camp somewhere far away on the edge of the world!!! No vacationers!!!||||We paid for one night and left immediately after breakfast.||||There was another couple from Colombia staying at this hotel, and they also left with us in search of a better hotel.||||Recommendation: Avoid this hotel. The reviews are either old or purchased. I've attached photos to prove my point. Don't ruin your vacation!!!||||Dear Booking and Tripadvisor, please lower this hotel's rating to "2."

textTranslated: The entire complex blends in well with the surrounding environment, although unfortunately a typical eco-monster is being built nearby. The buildings are new but built in colonial style and are nestled in a large park filled with tropical plants and flowers. Unfortunately, the materials used for construction, like the facade cladding, are plastic rather than wood, likely to keep maintenance costs low due to the proximity to the sea. Not all rooms and villas have a sea view, which in some cases is obscured by thick vegetation. They are tastefully furnished in a modern style and offer every comfort, starting with a comfortable queen-size bed. The only flaw we found was a loud, albeit intermittent, noise coming from the shower drain. There is a large, very nice swimming pool, unfortunately frequently populated by exuberant teenagers. The black sand beach overlooks a poorly sheltered stretch of sea, making it unsuitable for swimming due to both the waves and the rather strong currents. The main restaurant offers decent food but is penalized by disastrous service, the same goes for the poolside restaurant. Whether you're coming from the north or south, be prepared to travel several kilometers of very bumpy dirt road. There isn't much to do or see nearby; to escape the awful restaurant, we drove to San Juanillo, where there is a beautiful beach and a few bars with a bit of entertainment.

Las zonas comunes estaban sucias, había insectos por todas partes y varias de las piscinas estaban cerradas sin previo aviso. Para colmo, el personal de recepción fue muy borde y poco profesional, sin ofrecer soluciones ni mostrar interés por mejorar nuestra estancia.

No lo recomendaría en absoluto. El servicio deja mucho que desear y la limpieza brilla por su ausencia.
textTranslated:
Our experience at this hotel was extremely disappointing. Upon arrival, we found cockroaches in our room, so they had to move us. However, the new room was also in poor condition: the toilet kept getting clogged, and everything was generally malfunctioning.

The common areas were filthy, there were insects everywhere, and several of the pools were closed without prior notice. To top it all off, the reception staff were incredibly rude and unprofessional, offering no solutions and showing no interest in improving our stay.

I absolutely would not recommend this hotel. The service leaves much to be desired, and cleanliness is practically nonexistent.

address: 142, Provincia de Alajuela, La Fortuna, Costa Rica
name: James Niedens
text:
Favorite parts about our stay: the staff was so friendly, it was very private, great views of the volcano, their hot springs were great! Me and my wife were honeymooning and they left a plate of chocolate covered strawberries in our room. They also folded the towels into clever things which we always looked forward to when coming back to our room. (Elephant, flower girl) Breakfast was pretty good! They had papaya, pineapple, and watermelon almost everyday which was sweet, and they swapped between providing two types of juices: cas and cashew (? Not 100% sure on the second juice) and they were both very good. They had someone making omelets everyday which was a good change of things when their regular food wasn't as appetizing. They always had rice, scrambled eggs, some sort of potato, something sweet like pancakes or french toast. All of which were really tasty!

(I don't actually think their hot springs were real springs, more like hot tubs, but doesn't change the fact that they were really nice. And at least when me and my wife were their we barely saw anyone else using them)

Least favorite parts of our stay: The doors and windows in the walls were not sealed so a lot of bugs and a few lizards made their way into our room. (Half inch openings in some cases) We didn't have hot water for half our stay which was partly self inflicted because we didn't want to bother them about fixing it and we didn't want to be bothered. The food at the restaurant was good but a lot more expensive than the local sodas around and the restaurants in fortuna. We used a rental car so after the first night we went to fortuna for lunch and dinner and almost every single meal was half the cost of the food in the restaurant. We found a lot of places on google maps to be closed but by just driving around we found some really good places to eat. In case you're wondering, the wet bar (which we didn't use) looks like urine 😬 but again, we didn't use it so maybe it was clean.

All in all, I'm glad we stayed here! Safety was never a concern on my mind!
title: Hotel Arenal Paraíso Resort & Spa

Regresamos y nos dijeron que no nos pueden dar llave porque el sistema no funciona pero la mucama nos pueden abrir la habitación, tampoco tengo problema. Más tarde todavía no estaba lista la llave, ya se pone incómodo cada vez que quiero entrar a la habitación tengo que ir a la recepción a pedir que me abran. El problema de la llave fue resuelto a las 6pm para todos los huéspedes.
La habitación estandar, aislamiento de sonido nulo, puedo escuchar las conversaciones y cuando van al baño.
Desayuno de los 4 días son iguales todos los dias.
Las piscinas termales no todas estaban habilitadas, sin agua (da sensación de abandono, espero que sea otra causa). El agua deja de fluir después de las 6pm, lo cual convierte en agua estancada…
Lo único que se rescata es la ubicación del hotel, se ve el volcán sin ningún problema. Área verde bien mantenida y limpia, parqueo espacioso.
textTranslated:
The first day we arrived already cast a negative shadow over my perception of the hotel. They told us the room wasn't ready "yet," and to come back in an hour for the keys, no problem. We returned and were told they couldn't give us the key because the system wasn't working, but the maid could open the room for us, which was also fine. Later, the key still wasn't ready, and it's becoming inconvenient that every time I want to enter the room I have to go to reception to ask them to open it. The key problem was finally resolved at 6 pm for all guests.
The standard room had zero soundproofing; I could hear conversations and when people went to the bathroom. Breakfast was the same every day for all four days. Not all the thermal pools were open, and some were without water (giving a sense of neglect; I hope that's another reason). The water stops flowing after 6 pm, which turns it into stagnant water. The only redeeming feature is the hotel's location; you can see the volcano without any problem. Well-maintained and clean green area, spacious parking.
